model.name: Commercial Contract
model.purpose: Give agents the context needed to identify, form, read, operate and close a legally binding commercial agreement between two or more parties as a jointly owned record, independent of storage format.
model.scope_statement: Covers the agreement record itself: its identity and classification, the party positions and their authority, how it was concluded and executed, the structure and terms of the agreed text, the obligations and schedule it creates, the record of performance, non-performance, remedy, change, notice and termination, and the governance of that record (provenance, integrity, access, retention, interoperability). Scope is business-to-business commercial contracting, following the HCCH Principles' scope of parties acting in the exercise of their trade or profession. External legal norms, the real-world identity of the parties, procurement award processes and dispute proceedings are referenced, not duplicated.
in_scope: Agreement identity, subject-matter classification and the applicable legal regime declaration
Party positions, their roles, legal identification and signing authority
Formation facts: offer, acceptance, conduct, standard-term incorporation, execution and effectiveness
Addressable clause structure, constituent document set, precedence and authentic language
Commercial terms: price and payment, delivery and risk transfer, warranty, liability and protective terms
Obligations expressed as deontic specifications with bearers, source clauses, violations and reparations
Milestones, due conditions, cure periods and performance/acceptance records
Non-performance, excuse, remedy, amendment, assignment, notice, termination and survival
Record governance: provenance, integrity of the executed text, access, retention, disposition and projections
out_of_scope: Consumer contracts and employment contracts (excluded by the HCCH Principles' commercial scope)
The legal existence, powers and internal governance of the parties themselves (organization/person models)
The procurement or tendering process that precedes award
Conduct of litigation or arbitration proceedings and the resulting awards
Statutory and regulatory norms as such; only their declared applicability to this agreement is in scope
Payment execution, settlement instruments and accounting entries
Transfer of property/title, which CISG Article 4 expressly leaves to the applicable national law
Distributed-ledger execution substrates for smart contracts
Tax determination, transfer pricing and customs classification

boundary_notes.distinction: The tendering, evaluation and award process is owned by the procurement model; UBL separates Tender and Contract Award Notice documents from the resulting contract. Award output composes into a new agreement record here.

The legal entity and its verified identifier (LEI under ISO 17442) live in the party model; this model holds only the party position, its role and the link plus verification evidence. The registry validation flag 'a contract is not an organization' is upheld.

The arbitration or jurisdiction clause, the escalation state and the written-form evidence required by New York Convention Article II are in scope; the proceeding, award and enforcement action are not.

Overriding mandatory rules and statutory regimes (for example CISG applicability, unfair-term controls under the Data Act) are external norms; this model records only the applicability declaration and any opt-out.

Certificate issuance, trusted lists and signature-creation devices belong to the eIDAS trust-service domain; this model records the signature type, assurance level and validation evidence attached to execution.
Specialised agreement types EXTEND this model with domain terms and lifecycle events; their product-specific economics are not duplicated here.

sources.title: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (Vienna, 1980) (CISG)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
sources.relevance: Treaty structure supplies the canonical division into formation (Part II) and obligations, performance, breach, remedies and avoidance (Part III), plus Article 4 exclusion of property transfer and Article 11 freedom from writing requirements.

sources.title: UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts 2016
sources.organization: International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT)
sources.relevance: General restatement of commercial contract law covering formation, authority of agents, validity, interpretation, content, third-party rights, conditions, performance, hardship, non-performance, assignment and limitation periods; grounds obligation, excuse and remedy structure beyond sale of goods.

sources.title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0 (OASIS Standard)
sources.relevance: Normative vocabulary for deontic specifications (Obligation, Permission, Prohibition, Right), Bearer and AuxiliaryParty roles, Violation, Penalty and Reparation chains, and temporal characteristics of norms; used for the machine-readable obligation layer.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Naming Convention Version 1.0 (OASIS Standard)
sources.relevance: FRBR-based Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item IRI scheme and eId/wId attributes give stable addressing of clauses across amended versions of an agreed text.

sources.title: Principles on Choice of Law in International Commercial Contracts
sources.organization: Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH)
sources.relevance: Defines the commercial (non-consumer, non-employment) scope boundary, party autonomy, express versus tacit choice, severability of the choice-of-law clause and the scope of the chosen law over validity, interpretation, performance and remedies.

sources.title: Introducing the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) / ISO 17442
sources.version_or_date: ISO 17442 first published 2012; Part 2 published 2019; Global LEI Index current
sources.relevance: Governed 20-character global identifier for legal entities, supplying the authoritative party identifier and public verification source for party positions.

sources.title: eIDAS Regulation - electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by the European Digital Identity framework
sources.relevance: Regional legal effects of electronic signatures, seals, time stamps and registered delivery; source of signature assurance levels and qualified time-stamp evidence used in execution and notice findings.

sources.title: United Nations Convention on the Use of Electronic Communications in International Contracts (New York, 2005)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
sources.relevance: Rules on time and place of dispatch and receipt of electronic communications, location of parties, invitations to make offers, automated message systems and input errors; grounds the notice, conclusion-time and party-location data elements.

sources.title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures (2001)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
sources.relevance: Technology-neutral, reliability-based criteria for signature equivalence and the principles of non-discrimination and functional equivalence; the global counterweight to region-specific assurance tiers.

sources.title: Incoterms(R) Rules
sources.relevance: Controlled vocabulary of eleven three-letter delivery terms allocating tasks, costs and risk transfer between seller and buyer; requires an edition and a named place to be interpretable.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent model with wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, actedOnBehalfOf and generatedAtTime supplies the format-neutral provenance and audit-trail vocabulary.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile with mandatory seconds and an explicit Z or +/-hh:mm offset, and the -00:00 convention for unknown local offset; governs every contractual time value.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation - Records management - Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Records characteristics (authenticity, reliability, integrity, usability), metadata for records, and appraisal, retention and disposition concepts; grounds the record governance bundle.

sources.title: Data Act - Regulation (EU) 2023/2854
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854; in force 11 January 2024; applicable from 12 September 2025
sources.relevance: Regional control on unfair contractual terms unilaterally imposed in business-to-business data-sharing contracts, and essential requirements for smart contracts used to execute data-sharing agreements.

sources.title: Universal Business Language v2.4 approved as a Committee Specification
sources.version_or_date: UBL 2.4 Committee Specification, 27 October 2023; UBL 2.1 = ISO/IEC 19845:2015
sources.relevance: Ninety-three interoperable business document types including tendering and contracting documents; the reference projection target for exchanging contract-adjacent documents without exposing clause text.

sources.title: Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York, 1958)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
sources.relevance: Article II requires an arbitration agreement in writing and obliges courts to refer parties to arbitration; sets the evidentiary form requirement for the dispute-forum finding.

sources.title: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (Vienna, 1980) (CISG) — authentic English text
sources.relevance: Normative sales-contract code for formation, seller and buyer obligations, risk, damages, exemption, avoidance and preservation. Official UNCITRAL landing page: https://uncitral.un.org/en/texts/salegoods/conventions/sale_of_goods/cisg

sources.title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Machine-readable deontic, temporal, jurisdictional and isomorphic representation of norms including contracts: Obligation, Permission, Prohibition, Right, Violation, Penalty, Reparation, Bearer, Authority, Time.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 Part 1: XML Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Legal document identity (FRBR work/expression/manifestation/item), hierarchical provisions, metadata lifecycle, citations and naming. Namespace http://docs.oasis-open.org/legaldocml/ns/akn/3.0

sources.title: Uniform Commercial Code § 2-201 Formal Requirements; Statute of Frauds
sources.organization: American Law Institute / Uniform Law Commission
sources.version_or_date: UCC Article 2 as published on LII; retrieved 2026-08-25
sources.relevance: US-state commercial sales writing rule: $500 threshold, merchant confirmation exception, specially manufactured goods, admission and part-performance. Competes with CISG Article 11 where CISG applies and no Article 96 declaration is in force. Text published by the Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School.

sources.title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce (1996) with additional article 5 bis as adopted in 1998
sources.relevance: Non-discrimination, functional equivalence and technology neutrality for electronic information, writing and contracts. Companion to CISG Article 13 writing and to electronic formation. Published by the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law.

bundles.name: Identity and Legal Frame
bundles.description: What this agreement is, how it is uniquely denoted, what kind of transaction it governs and which law and forum apply to it.
bundles.rationale: Before any term can be read or any obligation operated, an agent must fix the record's identity boundary and the legal regime that determines validity, interpretation, performance and remedies; the HCCH Principles make the chosen law govern exactly those matters.

layers.name: Agreement Identity and Classification
layers.description: Denotation of the agreement instance and the coded classification that selects the applicable regime and term expectations.

findings.name: Agreement Record Identity and Instance Boundary
findings.description: How one agreement is distinguished from another, which identifier is authoritative, and where a framework agreement ends and a call-off begins.

questions.text: Which identifier is authoritative for this agreement, who issued it, and is it agreed by all parties?
Does this record denote one binding agreement, or a framework whose obligations arise only on call-off?
answer_data: Instance kind code (standalone, framework, call-off, schedule)

questions.text: How is a specific executed version of this agreement addressed as distinct from the abstract agreement?
If no master-system identifier exists, which Dimension minted the surrogate key and under what authority?

data_elements.name: agreementIdentifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the agreement instance, resolved by the identity priority rule.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Coded scheme of the identifier (master register, governed IRI, or Dimension-minted surrogate).

data_elements.name: parentAgreementRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the framework or master agreement under which this instance is concluded.

artifacts.name: Contract Register Entry
artifacts.description: The authoritative register record asserting the agreement identifier, its scheme, instance kind and links to parent or child instances.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Carries the authoritative master-system identifier where the register is the system of record; otherwise the governed IRI, with any Dimension-minted UUID/ULID recorded as an alias with minting provenance.

findings.name: Subject-Matter Classification and Applicable Regime
findings.description: Coded classification of what the agreement does, and the declared applicability or exclusion of regimes such as the CISG.

questions.text: What class of subject matter does the agreement govern, and under which classification scheme is that code drawn?
Are all parties acting in the exercise of their trade or profession, so that the commercial-contract scope applies?
Does the CISG or another uniform regime apply to this agreement, and has it been expressly excluded?
answer_data: Contracting-state status of each party's place of business

data_elements.name: subjectMatterClass
data_elements.description: Coded class of the transaction (sale of goods, services, licence, lease, distribution, data sharing).

data_elements.name: uniformRegimeApplicability
data_elements.description: Declared applicability or exclusion of a uniform regime such as the CISG, with the clause that effects the exclusion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is coded reference data asserted on the agreement record and resolved against external code lists; it produces no separate document. The evidence for a regime exclusion is the clause artifact already held by the clause-addressability finding, so duplicating an artifact here would fragment the executed text.

layers.name: Applicable Law and Dispute Forum
layers.description: The chosen governing law, the mandatory rules it cannot displace, and the forum agreed for disputes together with the form evidence that forum requires.

findings.name: Governing Law and Mandatory Rules
findings.description: Which law the parties chose, whether expressly or tacitly, the severability of that choice, and the overriding rules that apply regardless.

questions.text: Which law did the parties designate to govern the contract, and is the designation express or tacit?
Is the choice-of-law term recorded as severable, so that a defect in the main agreement does not invalidate it?
answer_data: Fallback conflict rule if choice fails

questions.text: Which overriding mandatory rules or unfair-term controls apply irrespective of the chosen law?
Does the chosen law cover interpretation, performance and remedies, or is the contract split across several laws?

data_elements.name: governingLaw
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction or body of law designated to govern the contract.

data_elements.name: choiceOfLawMode
data_elements.description: Whether the choice is express, tacit and clearly apparent, or absent so that conflict rules apply.

data_elements.name: overridingMandatoryRuleRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a rule that applies regardless of the chosen law, with the clauses it constrains.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The governing-law declaration is an attribute of the agreement plus a pointer into the executed clause tree; the clause text itself is the artifact of the clause-addressability finding. Minting a separate artifact would create a second, divergent copy of a normative provision.

findings.name: Dispute Forum, Escalation and Written-Form Evidence
findings.description: The agreed forum, escalation ladder and seat, plus the writing evidence an arbitration agreement needs to be enforceable across borders.

questions.text: Is the agreed forum a national court, an arbitral tribunal, or a staged escalation ending in one of them?
What evidence shows the arbitration agreement is in writing as required for cross-border enforcement?
What escalation stage has the dispute reached and when did each stage begin?
Under what condition does the forum obtain access to the otherwise confidential record?

data_elements.name: disputeForumType
data_elements.description: Coded forum agreed for disputes (court, institutional arbitration, ad hoc arbitration, expert determination).

data_elements.name: arbitralSeat
data_elements.description: Legal seat of arbitration determining the supervisory jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: escalationStage
data_elements.description: Current stage in the agreed dispute escalation ladder.

artifacts.name: Dispute Resolution Clause Extract
artifacts.description: Addressable extract of the jurisdiction or arbitration clause together with the writing evidence relied on for enforceability.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by the clause eId within the executed expression IRI; the extract carries a digest referencing the digest of the parent expression.

bundles.name: Parties, Identity and Authority
bundles.description: Who is bound, in what role, on whose behalf, and with what verified power to bind.
bundles.rationale: A contract binds legal persons through positions filled by representatives; UNIDROIT treats authority of agents as a distinct chapter and the LEI provides a governed identifier, so party position, party identity and signing authority are separable decision surfaces.

layers.name: Party Positions and Legal Identification
layers.description: The roles the agreement creates and the verified real-world entities that occupy them.

findings.name: Party Position and Contractual Role
findings.description: The abstract positions the agreement creates, their roles, and how liability is shared where several parties occupy one side.

questions.text: What role does each party position hold, and from which controlled vocabulary is the role code taken?
answer_data: Position label used in the text

questions.text: Where several obligors occupy one side, are their duties joint, several, or joint and several?
How is a party position kept distinct from the legal entity that currently occupies it?

data_elements.name: partyPositionId
data_elements.description: Identifier of a position in the agreement, stable across changes of the occupying entity.

data_elements.name: partyRoleCode
data_elements.description: Coded contractual role such as buyer, seller, licensor, supplier, guarantor.

data_elements.name: obligorPluralityMode
data_elements.description: How liability is shared among several obligors on the same side.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A party position is a structural slot in the agreement record, not a document. Its evidence is the executed text and the identity verification record held by the neighbouring finding; creating an artifact for a slot would assert a document that does not exist.

findings.name: Legal Identification and Place of Business
findings.description: The governed identifier for each party, the verification evidence behind it, and the place of business that drives regime applicability.

questions.text: Which governed global identifier denotes each party, and what is its current registration status?
What is each party's relevant place of business, and how was it determined where several exist?
What evidence supports the link between the named party in the text and the identified legal entity?
How is a party's change of name, registration or legal form recorded without breaking the position link?

data_elements.name: legalEntityIdentifier
data_elements.description: Twenty-character governed identifier of the legal entity occupying a party position, where available.

data_elements.name: placeOfBusiness
data_elements.description: Party's relevant place of business, used to determine uniform-regime applicability and communication rules.

data_elements.name: identityVerificationTime
data_elements.description: Observation time at which the party identity was last verified against the authoritative registry.

artifacts.name: Party Identity Verification Record
artifacts.description: Dated record of the check that ties the party named in the text to a registry entry, capturing method, source, result and verifier.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by party position identifier plus a zero-padded verification sequence number scoped to that position; carries the verified legal entity identifier as a foreign key.

layers.name: Authority and Representation
layers.description: The power of the individuals and intermediaries who bind the parties, and the positions of third parties who are affected without signing.

findings.name: Signing Authority and Capacity
findings.description: Who executed the agreement for each party, on what basis they were empowered, and what limits bounded that power.

questions.text: On what basis was each signatory empowered to bind the party, and where is that basis recorded?
What monetary, subject-matter or duration limits bound the signatory's authority at execution time?
If authority was exceeded, is the agreement treated as ratified, void, or binding on apparent authority?
Was signing authority verified before execution, by whom, and at what observation time?

data_elements.name: signingAuthorityBasis
data_elements.description: Coded basis of the signatory's power (statutory representative, board resolution, power of attorney, delegated mandate).

data_elements.name: authorityLimitAmount
data_elements.description: Monetary ceiling on the signatory's power, with its currency code.

artifacts.name: Authority Evidence Instrument
artifacts.description: The power of attorney, board resolution, register extract or delegation record relied on to show the signatory could bind the party.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing register's document number where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI, with a content digest binding it to the execution event.

findings.name: Agents, Guarantors and Third-Party Beneficiaries
findings.description: Positions held by parties who act for, secure or benefit from the agreement without being principal obligors.

questions.text: Which non-principal positions exist, and what right or exposure does each carry?
May a named beneficiary enforce a term directly, and can the parties vary it without that beneficiary's consent?
May an obligor perform through a subcontractor, and does the obligor remain liable for that performance?

data_elements.name: thirdPartyRoleCode
data_elements.description: Coded non-principal role such as agent, guarantor, beneficiary, subcontractor, escrow holder.

data_elements.name: beneficiaryRightEnforceable
data_elements.description: Whether a third-party beneficiary can enforce a conferred right directly.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Third-party positions are structural relations derived from the executed clauses; where a guarantee or agency is itself a separate agreement, it is a distinct instance of this model rather than an artifact of this finding, which avoids double-owning another contract's text.

bundles.name: Formation, Execution and Effectiveness
bundles.description: How the agreement came into existence, how consent was expressed and evidenced, and when it began to bite.
bundles.rationale: The CISG devotes a whole Part to formation by offer and acceptance, the UN electronic communications convention governs dispatch and receipt of the messages that carry consent, and eIDAS and the UNCITRAL Model Law govern the evidentiary weight of the resulting signature.

layers.name: Consent and Conclusion
layers.description: The offer, acceptance or conduct that concluded the agreement, and whose standard terms became part of it.

findings.name: Offer, Acceptance and Incorporated Standard Terms
findings.description: The communications and conduct that concluded the contract, when and where they took effect, and which standard terms were incorporated when both sides sent their own.

questions.text: By what act was the contract concluded: acceptance of a definite offer, conduct indicating assent, or an automated exchange?
At what dispatch and receipt times did the concluding communication take effect, in each party's offset?
Whose standard terms were incorporated, and how was a conflict between competing form sets resolved?
Was the proposal sufficiently definite as to goods, quantity and price for a binding contract to arise?

data_elements.name: conclusionMode
data_elements.description: Coded manner in which assent was expressed (signed instrument, offer and acceptance, conduct, automated system).

data_elements.name: conclusionEventTime
data_elements.description: Time at which the contract was concluded, recorded with seconds and explicit offset.

data_elements.name: incorporatedTermSetRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a standard term set incorporated by reference, with its version and the incorporation clause.

artifacts.name: Formation Communication Set
artifacts.description: The ordered set of pre-contractual communications (quotation, purchase order, order confirmation, acceptance message) relied on to show conclusion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each communication keyed by its transport message identifier where one exists, otherwise by a Dimension-minted ULID; ordered by a zero-padded sequence scoped to the agreement identifier.

layers.name: Execution and Effectiveness
layers.description: The signature or seal evidence attached to the agreed text, and the conditions that had to be met before it took effect.

findings.name: Execution, Signature Type and Form Requirement
findings.description: How the agreement was signed or sealed, the assurance level and validation evidence of that signature, and any form requirement it had to satisfy.

questions.text: Does any applicable rule require this agreement or a clause within it to be in writing or signed?
What signature or seal type was used by each signatory, and at what assurance level?
What validation evidence proves the signature was valid at signing time and remains verifiable now?
When and in which offset did each party execute, and which execution completed the agreement?

data_elements.name: executionTime
data_elements.description: Time at which a signatory executed, with seconds and the local offset of the place of execution preserved.

data_elements.name: signatureType
data_elements.description: Coded signature or seal type and its assurance level under the applicable trust framework.

data_elements.name: signedDataDigest
data_elements.description: Digest over the exact bytes covered by each signature, with the algorithm identifier.

artifacts.name: Signature Evidence Package
artifacts.description: The signed container, certificates, time-stamp tokens and validation report that together evidence execution and allow later re-verification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus signatory position and a zero-padded signature sequence; content-addressed by the digest of the signed bytes.

findings.name: Conditions Precedent, Effectiveness and Validity Defects
findings.description: The gap between execution and effect: conditions to be satisfied, approvals to be obtained, and defects that can unwind consent.

questions.text: Which conditions had to be satisfied or waived before obligations became enforceable, and what is each one's status?
How does the effective date differ from the execution date, and does any term apply retroactively?
Is any ground of invalidity asserted, such as mistake, fraud, threat or gross disparity, and by whom?
If a term is invalid or unenforceable, does the remainder of the agreement survive?

data_elements.name: effectiveDate
data_elements.description: Date or timestamp from which the agreement's obligations take effect.

data_elements.name: conditionPrecedent
data_elements.description: A condition to be satisfied or waived before effectiveness, with its status and evidence.

data_elements.name: validityStatus
data_elements.description: Current validity state of the agreement (effective, conditional, avoided, disputed).

findings.inline_only_rationale: Effectiveness is a computed state over conditions, clauses and events already held elsewhere; the documents that satisfy a condition (a regulatory approval, a guarantee) are artifacts owned by their own models or by the notice finding. Creating an artifact here would duplicate them.

bundles.name: Agreed Text and Commercial Terms
bundles.description: The structure of the agreed text, the documents that make it up, and the substantive commercial and protective terms it contains.
bundles.rationale: Operating a contract requires addressing individual provisions stably across amendments, knowing which documents govern when they conflict, and reading the price, delivery and protective terms as structured values rather than prose.

layers.name: Document Structure and Precedence
layers.description: How provisions are addressed, which documents constitute the contract, how conflicts between them resolve, and which language governs.

findings.name: Clause Addressability and Structure
findings.description: Stable identification of individual provisions across versions, their classification and their machine-readable form.

questions.text: How is a single provision addressed so the reference survives renumbering in a later amended version?
What functional class does a provision belong to, and which classification scheme assigns it?
What digest fixes the exact wording of a provision as executed?
Which machine-readable rule, if any, is asserted to represent this provision, and who asserted it?

data_elements.name: clauseExpressionId
data_elements.description: Expression-level identifier of a provision, valid within one version of the text.

data_elements.name: clauseWorkId
data_elements.description: Work-level identifier that persists across expressions, allowing a provision to be tracked through amendments.

data_elements.name: clauseClass
data_elements.description: Coded functional class of the provision (payment, liability, termination, confidentiality, governing law).

artifacts.name: Clause Tree Expression
artifacts.description: The hierarchical, addressable representation of one version of the agreed text with per-node identifiers and digests.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the FRBR expression IRI of the agreed text; each node addressed by its expression identifier, with the persistent work identifier retained for cross-version tracking.

findings.name: Constituent Documents, Precedence and Authentic Language
findings.description: Which documents together form the contract, how conflicts between them are ranked, and which language version controls.

questions.text: Which documents, schedules and incorporated term sets together constitute the contract?
In what rank order do the constituent documents prevail when their terms conflict?
Which language version is authentic, and what status do translations have?

data_elements.name: constituentDocumentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a document forming part of the contract, with its role and version.

data_elements.name: precedenceRank
data_elements.description: Ordinal rank of a constituent document in the agreed order of precedence.

data_elements.name: authenticLanguage
data_elements.description: Language code of the version that controls interpretation.

artifacts.name: Contract Document Manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest listing every constituent document with role, version, language, precedence rank and digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded manifest revision number; each entry carries the constituent document's own identifier and digest.

findings.name: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
findings.description: CISG Article 8 interprets statements and conduct first by a party's intent where the other party knew or could not have been unaware of it, otherwise by a reasonable person of the same kind in the same circumstances, having regard to negotiations, practices, usages and subsequent conduct. Article 9 binds parties to agreed usages and established practices and, unless otherwise agreed, to international trade usages they knew or ought to have known. Article 7 requires interpretation of the Convention itself with regard to international character, uniformity and good faith. UNIDROIT Chapter 4 (as part of PICC 2016) supplies complementary interpretation and gap-filling. These materials are evidence for meaning, not a second contract.

questions.text: For a disputed statement or clause, did the other party know or could it not have been unaware of the speaker's intent, and if not what would a reasonable person of the same kind have understood?
Which agreed usages, established practices between the parties, or widely known international trade usages are implied into the contract unless excluded?
What subsequent conduct of the parties is to be considered in interpretation, and which negotiation records are in the interpretation file rather than in the four corners of the instrument?

data_elements.name: stated_intent
data_elements.description: Intent of the party making the statement.

data_elements.name: known_to_counterparty
data_elements.description: Whether the other party knew or could not have been unaware of that intent.

data_elements.name: reasonable_person_reading
data_elements.description: Understanding of a reasonable person of the same kind in the same circumstances.

data_elements.name: negotiation_history_refs
data_elements.description: References to negotiation records used for interpretation.

data_elements.name: established_practices
data_elements.description: Practices established between the parties.

data_elements.name: agreed_usages
data_elements.description: Usages to which the parties have agreed.

data_elements.name: implied_international_usages
data_elements.description: International trade usages the parties knew or ought to have known.

data_elements.name: subsequent_conduct
data_elements.description: Subsequent conduct considered in interpretation.

data_elements.name: good_faith_issue
data_elements.description: Good-faith issue raised in interpretation under Article 7.

artifacts.name: Interpretation file
artifacts.description: Indexed negotiations, usages, practices and subsequent-conduct items used to interpret statements without rewriting the instrument.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier first, then any governed IRI, then a Dimension UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Commercial and Protective Terms
layers.description: Price and payment, delivery and risk, and the warranty, liability, confidentiality and compliance terms that allocate exposure.

findings.name: Price, Consideration and Payment Terms
findings.description: How the price is fixed or determined, in what currency, when payment falls due and what follows late payment.

questions.text: Is the price fixed, indexed, cost-plus, or determined by a mechanism, and what inputs drive it?
When does payment fall due relative to delivery, invoice or acceptance, and over what period?
What interest, charge or suspension right arises on late payment, and from which date does it run?
Is the price treated as restricted, so that it is withheld from non-party projections?

data_elements.name: priceBasis
data_elements.description: Coded method by which the contract price is determined.

data_elements.name: contractCurrency
data_elements.description: Currency code in which the price and payments are denominated.

data_elements.name: paymentPeriod
data_elements.description: Agreed period between the payment trigger and the due date.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Payment terms are structured values derived from clauses; the payment schedule itself is held by the milestone finding and the resulting invoices belong to a settlement model. Asserting a separate artifact here would either duplicate the clause text or claim ownership of financial documents outside this model's boundary.

findings.name: Delivery Terms, Risk Transfer and Conformity
findings.description: The trade term governing delivery and cost allocation, the point at which risk passes, and the conformity and inspection regime.

questions.text: Which trade term applies, of which edition, and to which named place or port?
At which event and moment does risk in the goods pass from seller to buyer?
Within what period must the goods or services be examined and non-conformity notified?
Where is the passing of property recorded, given that this model and the uniform sales regime exclude it?

data_elements.name: tradeTermCode
data_elements.description: Three-letter delivery term allocating tasks, costs and risk between seller and buyer.

data_elements.name: tradeTermEdition
data_elements.description: Edition of the trade-term rule set, without which the code is ambiguous.

data_elements.name: riskTransferEvent
data_elements.description: Event and location at which risk passes, with its recorded timestamp.

artifacts.name: Delivery and Conformity Evidence
artifacts.description: Transport, handover and inspection documents evidencing delivery, the moment of risk transfer and the conformity of what was delivered.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the issuing system's document number where one exists, otherwise by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded delivery sequence; each record cites the obligation it discharges.

findings.name: Warranty, Liability, Confidentiality and Compliance Terms
findings.description: Terms that allocate risk and constrain conduct: warranties, liability caps and exclusions, indemnities, confidentiality, intellectual property, data protection and fairness controls.

questions.text: What ceiling and exclusions limit each party's liability, and which heads of loss are carved out?
What is warranted, for how long, and what is the exclusive remedy for a warranty breach?
What information is confidential, for how long after termination, and which disclosures are permitted?
Has any term been screened as unilaterally imposed and potentially unfair under applicable controls?

data_elements.name: liabilityCapAmount
data_elements.description: Maximum aggregate liability of a party, with currency and the basis of calculation.

data_elements.name: warrantyPeriod
data_elements.description: Duration for which a warranty is given, and the event from which it runs.

data_elements.name: unfairTermScreenResult
data_elements.description: Outcome of screening a clause against applicable unfair-term controls.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are structured readings of clauses already carried by the clause tree artifact. Holding them as separate artifacts would create a normatively significant second copy of contract wording whose divergence from the executed text could not be detected.

bundles.name: Obligations, Performance and Variance
bundles.description: What the agreement requires, when it falls due, what actually happened, and how the parties change or end it.
bundles.rationale: The uniform sales regime and the UNIDROIT Principles both organise the operative life of a contract around obligations, performance, non-performance, excuse and remedy; LegalRuleML supplies the machine-readable deontic form of those duties.

layers.name: Obligations and Schedule
layers.description: The duties the agreement creates and the temporal conditions that make them performable or overdue.

findings.name: Obligation as Deontic Specification
findings.description: Each duty expressed with its deontic type, bearer, auxiliary party, source clause and the violation and reparation that follow non-compliance.

questions.text: Is this norm an obligation, a permission, a prohibition or a right, and who bears it?
Which provision creates this duty, and does any other provision qualify or defeat it?
What counts as violation of this duty, and what penalty or reparation is chained to it?
What is the current state of the duty: not yet due, due, performed, waived, or violated?

data_elements.name: obligationId
data_elements.description: Identifier of a single duty derived from the agreement.

data_elements.name: deonticType
data_elements.description: Coded deontic operator classifying the norm.

data_elements.name: bearerPartyPosition
data_elements.description: Party position legally bound by the norm.

data_elements.name: obligationStatus
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the duty.

artifacts.name: Machine-Readable Obligation Rule Set
artifacts.description: Derived, versioned set of deontic statements with bearers, conditions, violations and reparations, each traced to a source clause identifier.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded derivation revision; each norm carries its own identifier and a link to the source clause work-level identifier so it survives amendment.

findings.name: Milestones, Due Conditions and Cure Periods
findings.description: The calendar and event conditions that make a duty performable or overdue, together with grace and cure periods.

questions.text: Is the duty triggered by a fixed date, an elapsed period, or the occurrence of another event?
How long is any grace or cure period, and from which notice or event does it run?
Is timely performance treated as essential, so that delay alone justifies avoidance?
Which milestones depend on the completion of others, and what happens when an upstream one slips?

data_elements.name: dueTimestamp
data_elements.description: Moment at which a duty becomes due, recorded with seconds and explicit offset.

data_elements.name: curePeriod
data_elements.description: Additional period allowed to remedy a failure before consequences apply.

data_elements.name: milestoneAcceptanceCriteria
data_elements.description: Criteria a deliverable must satisfy at a milestone for performance to be accepted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Milestones are computed projections over obligations, dates and events. Any published schedule is a projection artifact governed by the interoperability finding; a standalone schedule artifact here would risk becoming an authoritative timetable that diverges from the clauses that generate it.

layers.name: Performance and Non-Performance
layers.description: What was rendered and accepted, and what happens when performance fails, is excused or triggers a remedy.

findings.name: Performance Record, Measurement and Acceptance
findings.description: Evidence that a duty was performed, the measured result against agreed criteria, and the counterparty's acceptance or rejection.

questions.text: What evidence shows that a specific obligation was performed, and who produced it?
Against which agreed metric was performance measured, and what value was observed?
Did the counterparty accept, reject or accept with reservations, and within what period?
When did performance actually occur, and when was it recorded in the system?

data_elements.name: performanceEventTime
data_elements.description: Time at which performance was actually rendered.

data_elements.name: performanceObservationTime
data_elements.description: Time at which the performance fact was observed or ingested into the record.

data_elements.name: acceptanceState
data_elements.description: Counterparty's acceptance decision on rendered performance.

data_elements.name: measuredPerformanceValue
data_elements.description: Observed value of an agreed performance metric, with its unit and target.

artifacts.name: Acceptance Certificate or Performance Evidence Record
artifacts.description: The signed acceptance certificate, service report or equivalent record asserting that a duty was discharged and on what measured basis.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded performance record sequence; carries the discharged obligation identifier and a digest of any attached evidence.

findings.name: Non-Performance, Excuse and Remedy
findings.description: Declared failure to perform, its severity, any excuse such as impediment or hardship, and the remedy elected or agreed.

questions.text: Is the non-performance fundamental, so that avoidance is available, or merely a delay or defect?
Is an excuse asserted on grounds of impediment beyond control or of hardship, and with what evidence?
Which remedy has the aggrieved party elected: performance, price reduction, damages, or avoidance?
How is the claimed loss quantified, and is it capped or liquidated by an agreed term?

data_elements.name: nonPerformanceDeclarationTime
data_elements.description: Time at which non-performance was formally declared.

data_elements.name: excuseGround
data_elements.description: Coded ground on which performance is excused or renegotiation is sought.

data_elements.name: remedyKind
data_elements.description: Coded remedy elected or agreed in response to non-performance.

data_elements.name: claimAmount
data_elements.description: Monetary amount claimed, with currency and quantification basis.

artifacts.name: Breach Declaration and Remedy Record
artifacts.description: The declaration of non-performance, any impediment notice, the remedy election and any settlement of the claim between the parties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded claim sequence; linked to the affected obligation identifiers and to the notice artifact that communicated it.

findings.name: Breach, additional time, cure, suspension and anticipatory breach
findings.description: CISG Article 25 defines fundamental breach as detriment that substantially deprives the other party of what it is entitled to expect, unless the result was not foreseeable. Articles 47 and 63 allow a Nachfrist additional period of reasonable length; during it the fixing party may not resort to inconsistent remedies but keeps damages for delay. Articles 71–72 allow suspension for apparent future non-performance of a substantial part, with immediate notice and a duty to continue if adequate assurance is provided, and avoidance for clear future fundamental breach. Article 73 deals with instalments. LegalRuleML Violation, Suborder, Penalty and Reparation model the deontic consequence of breach. A breach declaration is a party event, not a court judgment; adjudication is a sibling process.

questions.text: Has a party declared a breach, is it fundamental under CISG Article 25, and was the detriment foreseeable to a reasonable person in the same circumstances?
Has an additional period of reasonable length been fixed, what is its end time, and has the non-performing party offered cure that must be allowed to run?
Has performance been suspended for apparent future non-performance or avoided for clear future fundamental breach, was notice given, and was adequate assurance provided?
If the contract is an instalment contract, does the breach justify avoidance of one instalment, of future instalments, or of interdependent past deliveries as well?

data_elements.name: breach_declaration_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the breach declaration.

data_elements.name: linked_obligation_id
data_elements.description: Obligation said to be breached.

data_elements.name: fundamental_breach_flag
data_elements.description: Whether the breach is fundamental under CISG Article 25.

data_elements.name: foreseeability_finding
data_elements.description: Finding on foreseeability of the detriment.

data_elements.name: nachfrist_period
data_elements.description: Additional period of reasonable length fixed for performance.

data_elements.name: cure_offer
data_elements.description: Offer of cure by the non-performing party.

data_elements.name: suspension_notice_time
data_elements.description: Time notice of suspension was given.

data_elements.name: assurance_offered
data_elements.description: Adequate assurance of performance offered.

data_elements.name: anticipatory_flag
data_elements.description: Whether the declaration concerns future non-performance.

data_elements.name: instalment_scope
data_elements.description: Scope of avoidance across instalments.

artifacts.name: Breach and cure docket
artifacts.description: Declared breaches, Nachfrist notices, cure offers, suspension and assurance exchanges, with event times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier first, then any governed IRI, then a Dimension UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Change, Communication and Closure
layers.description: Amendment of the terms, transfer of positions, the formal notices that operate the contract, and the way it ends.

findings.name: Amendment and Variation
findings.description: Agreed changes to the terms, the formality they require, the clauses they touch and the version they produce.

questions.text: Which provisions does the amendment insert, replace or delete, and what new expression results?
What formality does the contract require for a variation to be effective, and was it met?
From when does the amendment take effect, and does it apply to obligations already due?
How does a reader of an old clause reference reach the corresponding provision in the amended text?

data_elements.name: amendmentId
data_elements.description: Identifier of an executed amendment instrument.

data_elements.name: amendmentEffectiveTime
data_elements.description: Time from which the amended terms take effect.

data_elements.name: affectedClauseRefs
data_elements.description: Work-level identifiers of provisions changed by the amendment.

artifacts.name: Executed Amendment Instrument
artifacts.description: The signed instrument recording an agreed change, with its own execution evidence and the resulting consolidated expression.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded amendment sequence that is never reused; the consolidated text is addressed by a new expression IRI whose effective date is a separate field rather than the identifier.

findings.name: Assignment, Novation and Change of Control
findings.description: Transfer of rights or of a whole position to a successor, the consent it requires, and its effect on the record's continuity.

questions.text: Is the transfer an assignment of rights, a transfer of obligations, or a novation of the whole position?
Whose consent was required for the transfer, and what evidences that consent?
Does a change of control of a party trigger a notification duty or a termination right?
After transfer, does the party position identifier persist while the occupying entity changes?

data_elements.name: transferKind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of transfer affecting a party position or its rights.

data_elements.name: successorEntityRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the legal entity taking over the position, with its governed identifier.

data_elements.name: transferEffectiveTime
data_elements.description: Time from which the transfer takes effect between the parties.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Where the transfer is documented, that document is an executed amendment or a separate agreement instance and is already covered by those findings. Recording a duplicate artifact here would create two independent chains of title over the same position.

findings.name: Notices and Formal Communication
findings.description: The formal messages that operate the contract, the channels and addresses they must use, and the rules that deem them received.

questions.text: Which channels and addresses are valid for a formal notice under this contract?
When was the notice dispatched and when is it deemed received under the agreed or default rule?
What kind of notice is this, and which contractual consequence does it start?
What evidence proves delivery of the notice to the designated address?

data_elements.name: noticeKind
data_elements.description: Coded type of formal notice (breach, cure demand, impediment, termination, renewal, address change).

data_elements.name: noticeDispatchTime
data_elements.description: Time at which the notice left the sender's control.

data_elements.name: noticeDeemedReceiptTime
data_elements.description: Time at which the notice is treated as received under the agreed or default rule.

artifacts.name: Notice and Delivery Evidence
artifacts.description: The notice as sent together with transport or registered-delivery evidence establishing dispatch and receipt.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded notice sequence; retains the transport message identifier and a digest of the notice content as sent.

findings.name: Termination, Expiry and Survival
findings.description: How the agreement ends, on what ground, which provisions survive and what wind-down obligations remain.

questions.text: Did the agreement end by full performance, expiry of term, notice, avoidance for breach, or mutual release?
Which provisions survive the end of the agreement, and for how long?
What wind-down duties remain: return or deletion of materials, final accounting, transition assistance?
What status does the record take after termination, and when does it become eligible for disposition?

data_elements.name: agreementEndMode
data_elements.description: Coded manner in which the agreement came to an end.

data_elements.name: endEffectiveTime
data_elements.description: Time from which the agreement ceased to be in force.

data_elements.name: survivingClauseRefs
data_elements.description: Identifiers of provisions that continue in force after the end of the agreement.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Termination is effected by a notice, an expiry of term, or an amendment-like release, all of which are already held as artifacts by the notice and amendment findings. The end state itself is a derived status over those events plus the clause tree.

bundles.name: Record Governance, Evidence and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the jointly owned record stays trustworthy, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it is exchanged without leaking terms.
bundles.rationale: Records management standards make authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability the defining properties of a record and require metadata and disposition control; provenance vocabulary and interchange standards make those properties expressible across systems.

layers.name: Provenance and Integrity
layers.description: Attribution of every assertion in the record and cryptographic fixity of the executed text.

findings.name: Provenance, Attribution and Text Integrity
findings.description: Who or what generated each assertion, from which source it was derived, when, and what digest and signature evidence fixes the executed text against later alteration.

questions.text: Which agent is responsible for each assertion in the record, and on whose behalf did it act?
From which source document or message was each derived value obtained, and by what method?
Are the time the contractual fact occurred and the time it entered the record kept distinct throughout?
How is the executed text verified as unaltered, and what happens when verification fails?

data_elements.name: generatingAgent
data_elements.description: Agent responsible for producing an assertion or artifact in the record.

data_elements.name: derivedFromRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the entity from which a recorded value was derived.

data_elements.name: ingestionTime
data_elements.description: Time at which an assertion was generated in or ingested into the record, distinct from the event time it describes.

data_elements.name: recordDigest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical bytes of an artifact or expression, with its algorithm identifier.

artifacts.name: Provenance and Audit Log
artifacts.description: Append-only, tamper-evident log of activities, agents, derivations, digests and access events over the agreement record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Entries keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded monotonic sequence; each segment chained to the digest of the preceding segment so gaps are detectable.

layers.name: Access, Retention and Exchange
layers.description: Confidentiality of the joint record, its disposition over time, and the projections through which it interoperates.

findings.name: Access, Disclosure and Redaction
findings.description: Who may read which part of the joint record, under what grant and purpose, and how compelled disclosure is handled.

questions.text: Which grant permits a reader to see a given bundle, layer, finding or artifact, and for what purpose?
On what grounds may the record be disclosed to a forum, regulator or auditor without party consent?
Which elements must be redacted before disclosure outside the parties, and how is redaction proven complete?
Which facts are joint, so that no single party may change or release them unilaterally?

data_elements.name: accessGrantRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the grant authorising a reader's access to a scoped part of the record.

data_elements.name: disclosureScope
data_elements.description: Coded scope of what a given recipient may see.

data_elements.name: jointFactFlag
data_elements.description: Marks an element as jointly owned, requiring joint evidence to change.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Access grants are governed records owned by the access-grant model and referenced here; the evidence of each access is an entry in the provenance and audit log artifact. A separate artifact would fork authority over grants away from their owning model.

findings.name: Retention, Limitation Periods and Disposition
findings.description: How long the record must be kept, what suspends deletion, and how authorised disposition is carried out and evidenced.

questions.text: Which event starts the retention clock, and what period applies to each class of element?
What limitation period governs claims under this agreement, and does it exceed the retention period?
Is a legal hold or dispute suspending disposition, who imposed it, and when may it be lifted?
How is a personal-data erasure request reconciled with the duty to preserve executed contractual evidence?

data_elements.name: retentionPeriod
data_elements.description: Period for which an element class must be retained after the trigger event.

data_elements.name: legalHoldFlag
data_elements.description: Indicates that disposition is suspended for the element while a hold is in force.

data_elements.name: dispositionTime
data_elements.description: Time at which authorised disposition was carried out.

artifacts.name: Disposition and Hold Record
artifacts.description: Record of retention rules applied, holds imposed and lifted, and disposition actions carried out with their authorising instrument.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by agreement identifier plus a zero-padded disposition sequence; cites the disposition authority reference and the digests of anything destroyed or redacted.

findings.name: External Alignment and Projections
findings.description: Declared alignments to external vocabularies and the reduced views published to non-parties, with what each view omits.

questions.text: Which external vocabularies are aligned to this model, and is the claim alignment or tested conformance?
What does each published projection expose, and which elements does it deliberately omit?
Where two aligned standards model the same concept differently, which mapping governs and why?
How current is a published projection, and at what observation time was it generated?

data_elements.name: alignmentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to an external standard or vocabulary this model is mapped to, with its version.

data_elements.name: conformanceClaimLevel
data_elements.description: Declared strength of the relationship to an external standard (aligned, partially conformant, conformant with evidence).

data_elements.name: projectionDefinition
data_elements.description: Definition of a published view, listing exposed and omitted elements and its audience.

artifacts.name: Projection and Alignment Map
artifacts.description: Governed document listing each published projection with its exposed and omitted elements, and each external mapping with its claim level and evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a governed IRI under the model namespace plus a zero-padded revision number; each mapping entry cites the external standard's own versioned identifier.

functions.name: Register agreement record
functions.description: Create the jointly owned record for a new agreement with its identifier, party positions, classification and legal frame.
inputs: Party position set with role codes
preconditions: At least two party positions are declared
A commercial-scope assertion exists for every position
Governing law and forum are declared or explicitly marked absent
effects: Agreement identifier is bound and cannot be reassigned
Record enters the pre-effective state
Registration event is written to the audit log with event and ingestion time

functions.name: Verify party identity and signing authority
functions.description: Check each named party against the authoritative registry and confirm the signatory's power to bind within its limits.
preconditions: A party position exists
An authority basis is asserted
effects: Verification observation time is recorded
Authority defect raises an exception state instead of blocking silently

functions.name: Record conclusion and execution
functions.description: Capture the concluding communications or signatures, the effective moment and the signature validation evidence.
inputs: Formation communication set or signed container
preconditions: Party identity and authority verification have been attempted and their results recorded
Any applicable form requirement has been identified
effects: Executed expression digest is fixed and becomes immutable
Record moves to conditional or effective state depending on outstanding conditions

functions.name: Build addressable clause tree
functions.description: Convert the agreed text into a hierarchy of addressable provisions with expression and work identifiers and per-node digests.
preconditions: The manifestation's digest matches the executed expression digest
effects: Clause references become stable across later amendments
Any extraction uncertainty is recorded as provenance, not silently normalised

functions.name: Derive obligation set
functions.description: Produce deontic statements with bearers, conditions, violations and reparations traced to source clauses.
preconditions: Clause tree exists with stable identifiers
Bearer positions are resolvable
effects: Derived rules are marked as derived, never as the normative text
A later amendment invalidates and re-derives the affected rules

functions.name: Evaluate effectiveness and conditions
functions.description: Determine whether conditions precedent are satisfied or waived and compute the current validity state.
preconditions: Execution has been recorded
Each condition has an evidence slot
effects: Obligations become enforceable only after the effectiveness event
Lapse at long-stop date is recorded as an event, not a deletion

functions.name: Monitor due obligations
functions.description: Compute which duties are due, overdue or within a cure period from due conditions and recorded events.
preconditions: Obligations carry due conditions
All timestamps carry seconds and explicit offsets
effects: Status transitions are emitted as events with event and observation time
No status is inferred without an evidenced trigger

functions.name: Record performance and acceptance
functions.description: Attach evidence that a duty was performed, capture measured results and register the counterparty's acceptance decision.
preconditions: The obligation exists and is due or performable
The recording actor is authorised for that party position
effects: Event time and observation time are stored separately
Deemed acceptance is applied only where an agreed rule exists

functions.name: Declare non-performance and elect remedy
functions.description: Register a breach declaration, any asserted excuse, the remedy elected and its quantification.
preconditions: A notice satisfying the contractual notice rules has been issued where required
Any cure period has expired or is expressly waived
effects: Record enters a disputed state that blocks disposition
Remedy election is immutable once notified, subject to a superseding agreed settlement

functions.name: Apply executed amendment
functions.description: Produce a new expression of the agreed text from an executed amendment while retaining the superseded expression.
preconditions: The required variation formality is satisfied and evidenced
The amendment is signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution
effects: Superseded expression is retained and remains addressable
Obligations affected by changed clauses are invalidated and re-derived

functions.name: Issue and track formal notice
functions.description: Send a contractual notice through a permitted channel to the designated address and record dispatch, receipt and consequences.
preconditions: The channel and address are permitted by the contract
The sender is authorised to act for the sending position
effects: Notice periods start running from the deemed receipt time
Failure of delivery evidence marks the notice as contested rather than valid

functions.name: Verify record integrity
functions.description: Re-verify digests, signatures and time stamps over the executed text and dependent artifacts and report divergence.
preconditions: A canonicalisation rule is recorded for each artifact class
effects: Failed verification sets a disputed flag and never deletes the artifact
Verification observation time is recorded separately from the artifact's event time

functions.name: Emit projection to a non-party
functions.description: Generate a reduced view exposing only the elements a declared projection permits, with its omission list and generation time.
preconditions: A valid, unexpired grant covers the requested scope
The projection definition is a governed, versioned artifact
effects: Restricted elements are excluded before serialisation, not filtered afterwards
Every emission is logged with requester, purpose and grant reference

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Evaluate retention rules, limitation periods and holds, and carry out authorised disposition or redaction with evidence.
inputs: Limitation period for the governing law
preconditions: No hold or dispute is in force over the element
The longest applicable retention or limitation period has expired
effects: Executed text and signature evidence are never hard-deleted while any period runs
Redaction preserves the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control

functions.name: Avoid or terminate
functions.description: End the agreement by notice of avoidance, agreed termination or expiry, releasing future duties while preserving dispute and winding-up clauses and triggering restitution.
preconditions: fundamental breach, Nachfrist failure, agreed termination, or completed performance
notice given where CISG Article 26 requires it
effects: status becomes avoided or terminated
open primary obligations are released subject to damages and restitution

functions.name: Declare breach and fix additional time
functions.description: Record a breach declaration, classify it as fundamental or not, and optionally fix a Nachfrist period or demand adequate assurance.
preconditions: failure to perform or clear future fundamental breach
notice capable of reaching the other party
effects: inconsistent remedies are barred during a running Nachfrist
damages for delay remain available

functions.name: Assign or novate
functions.description: Transfer rights or, with required consent, obligations, and notify the remaining obligor without purporting to move in rem title.
preconditions: contractual assignability or required consent
notice to obligor where effectiveness against the obligor so requires
effects: party positions or payee identity change on the contractual plane only

composition.target: world.organization (O1)
composition.purpose: Resolve the legal entity occupying a party position and its governed identifier; entity existence and powers stay in the organization model.

composition.target: world.person (H1)
composition.purpose: Resolve natural persons acting as signatories or agents without duplicating personal data in the contract record.

composition.target: world.charter (O4)
