owner_package_requirements: Declare a jointly owned record package per agreement instance in which each party position holds an equivalent mirror and joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events; unilateral acts such as notices are writable by their sender alone.
Bind every party position to an authoritative party record and store the identity verification evidence with its observation time before any obligation is derived.
Declare governing law, dispute forum and the retention jurisdiction before clause content is stored, because these determine mandatory rules, limitation periods and deletion limits.
Publish an AGENTS.md bootstrap and a versioned projection catalogue listing every view exposed to non-parties and what each view omits.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Adopt the namespace world.commercialContract under nav path NAV.SOC.ECO.CTR. Agreement expressions and clauses are named with FRBR-style Work and Expression IRIs and persistent clause identifiers so that references survive amendment; never mint contract IRIs under a single party's namespace, because the record is jointly owned. Derived artifacts such as obligation rule sets live in a clearly separate derived subnamespace so they can never be mistaken for the executed text.
registry_links: Global LEI Index for party legal entity identifiers under ISO 17442
ICC Incoterms rule codes with an explicit edition qualifier
Currency and country code lists referenced by the price, place-of-business and jurisdiction elements
Trusted lists of qualified trust service providers for signature and time-stamp validation
UBL document type and business process code lists used by exchange projections

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the executed expression: the clause tree with stable identifiers, the party positions, the derived obligation set marked as derived, and a digest over the normative text. PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, JSON, YAML and database rows are manifestations, not the canon.

Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; the local offset of execution, dispatch and delivery is preserved rather than normalised to Z, because contractual periods run in a stated locality.
Monetary values are canonicalised as an amount plus a currency code, never as formatted strings; quantities carry an explicit unit.
Parties are canonicalised to a position identifier plus a governed entity identifier, never to a display name; trade terms are canonicalised as code plus edition plus named place.
patch_rules: A patch that changes normative text is valid only if it carries an executed amendment instrument signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution.
Patches are append-only: superseded expressions are retained and remain addressable by their expression IRI; no in-place overwrite of executed content is permitted.
Editorial or metadata patches must be flagged non-normative and must not change the digest of the executed expression; if the digest would change, the change is an amendment, not a patch.
Every patch records the actor, the reason, the event time at which the change takes effect and the ingestion time at which it was recorded, as distinct values.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional findings, data elements or projections is backward compatible; changing the clause identity scheme, the deontic vocabulary, the party role vocabulary or the identity priority is breaking and requires a major version.
Relationships to CISG, UNIDROIT, Incoterms, UBL, LegalRuleML and Akoma Ntoso are published as alignments with a declared claim level; a conformance claim requires cited test evidence.
Consumers must tolerate unknown clause classes, unknown remedy kinds and unknown notice kinds rather than rejecting the record, and must not infer absence of a term from absence of a code.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the agreement, such as the contract register number of the register the parties have jointly designated as authoritative, where such an identifier exists and is agreed by all parties
Governed global identifier or IRI, such as a FRBR-style Akoma Ntoso expression IRI for the executed text or an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier for a party occupying a position
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting authority and mint time, used only where neither a master-system nor a governed identifier is available
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-times carrying seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; the local offset of execution, dispatch, delivery and performance is preserved because contractual periods run in a stated locality. Event time, meaning the moment the contractual fact occurred or took effect, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the moment the record captured it, whenever the two can differ. Where UTC is known but the local offset is not, use -00:00 rather than Z. A date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely amendments, notices, performance records, verification records, manifests, dispositions and log segments, are numbered with a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to the agreement identifier and the artifact class, for example agreement-id/amendment/0003. Sequence numbers are never reused, never renumbered on amendment and never encode a date; any effective date is carried as a separate field.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every executed or issued artifact carries a digest over its canonical bytes with a named algorithm, the signature or seal evidence relied on at execution, and an attributable time stamp. The digest of the executed expression is immutable for the life of the record. Verification failure sets a disputed flag, notifies all party positions and is written to the audit log; it never causes deletion or silent replacement of the artifact.

policies: Joint record policy: the agreement record is jointly owned by the party positions; joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events, while unilateral acts are attributable to their sender and remain contestable by the counterparty.
Alignment-not-conformance policy: relationships to external standards are recorded as alignments with an explicit claim level; a conformance claim without cited test evidence is a defect.

Derived-content policy: obligation rule sets, schedules, scorecards and summaries are marked as derived and carry provenance back to source clauses; they never acquire normative status over the executed text.
Minimisation policy: any view issued to a non-party exposes only what its versioned projection definition permits and publishes the list of what it omits.

Preservation policy: retention rules are suspended by a dispute or legal hold; personal data inside executed evidence is redacted in place with preserved digests rather than destroyed while any limitation period runs.
Party-mirror policy: each party holds the full agreement record; joint facts change only by joint events or jointly authorized amendments.

Form-and-signature policy: writing and signature requirements follow the applicable instrument (CISG Articles 11–13 and 96, UCC § 2-201, MLEC/MLES) and any insisted particular form under UNIDROIT Article 2.1.13.
Disclosure-minimisation policy: existence and performance standing may be disclosed to consented credit or rating consumers; clause text and prices are omitted from public summaries.
No-unilateral-delete policy: the joint record is not deleted by a single party's CRUD delete; retention, legal hold and limitation clocks govern archive and redaction.

read: Every party position may read the complete joint record, including clause text, obligations and performance history.
Non-parties read only through a declared projection, and the projection definition is itself a governed, versioned artifact.
Reads of restricted findings such as price terms, liability caps and personal data are logged with requester identity, purpose and grant reference.
create: Creating an agreement record requires at least two party positions, a subject-matter class, a governing-law declaration and a recorded conclusion or execution event with evidence.
Clause, obligation, milestone, performance, notice and amendment records may be created only under an existing agreement identifier.
Creation resolves the identifier through the identity priority; a Dimension-minted surrogate is permitted only with recorded minting authority and mint time.
update: Changes to normative content require an executed amendment artifact; the prior expression is retained and stays addressable.
Operational changes such as performance, notices, status transitions and disclosures are recorded as append-only events, never as in-place edits.
Metadata corrections are recorded as non-normative patches carrying actor, reason, event time and ingestion time, and must not alter the executed expression digest.
delete: Hard deletion of executed text, signature evidence, notices or performance evidence is prohibited while any limitation period, statutory retention duty or legal hold applies.
Personal data within executed evidence may be redacted in place, with a redaction record preserving the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control.
Disposition after retention expiry follows an approved disposition authority and is itself recorded as an event with its authorising instrument.

roles.name: Party record steward
responsibilities: Maintain one party's mirror of the joint record and keep it reconciled with the counterparty's mirror
Escalate divergence between mirrors as a dispute rather than resolving it unilaterally

roles.name: Authorised representative
responsibilities: Execute, amend, assign or terminate on behalf of a party within recorded authority limits
Ensure the authority instrument relied on is current and evidenced at the time of signing

roles.name: Contract text custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the clause tree, expression versions, document manifest and precedence order
Preserve superseded expressions and the identifier map that links them

roles.name: Performance recorder and verifier
responsibilities: Record performance events, measured values and acceptance decisions with event and observation times
Attach evidence and flag deemed acceptance only where an agreed rule exists

roles.name: Access and disclosure administrator
responsibilities: Issue, scope and expire grants over bundles, layers, findings and artifacts
Apply redaction rules and log every disclosure with purpose and legal basis

roles.name: Records and retention officer
responsibilities: Apply retention rules, limitation periods and legal holds and block disposition while any is in force
Execute and evidence authorised disposition or redaction

access.default_rule: Deny by default to anyone who is not a party position. Each party position has full read of the joint record, write on its own unilateral acts, and no unilateral write on joint facts, which require joint evidence.
exceptions: Adjudication access: a court or arbitral tribunal obtains the record once a dispute is escalated under the agreed forum clause
Regulatory or tax authority access on a stated legal basis, with the parties notified unless notification is prohibited
Auditor, financier or prospective assignee due diligence under a time-limited grant, normally on a redacted projection
Statutory disclosure duties, including unfair-term and data-sharing controls, that override a confidentiality clause
Emergency continuity access by a designated custodian where a party's system is unavailable, logged and reviewed afterwards
Adjudication access after a dispute is escalated to the contractual forum
Consented counterparty-status disclosure of existence and coarse performance standing to credit or rating consumers
Public-summary projection of existence, parties and subject-matter class where a transparency register is agreed or required
Mandatory regulatory disclosure that is an overriding mandatory rule of the forum
audit_requirements: Log every read of a restricted finding or artifact with requester, purpose, grant reference and timestamp carrying an explicit offset
Log grant issuance, scope, expiry and revocation as first-class events
Keep the audit log append-only and tamper-evident, with each segment chained to the digest of its predecessor
Retain audit entries at least as long as the record element they describe, and never dispose of them earlier

Log execution, amendment, performance acceptance, breach declaration, avoidance, assignment and every access exception with actor, artifact, event time and ingestion time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Preserve content hashes of each expression so that later projections can be verified
Record who opened adjudication access and under which dispute-clause identifier

required_fields: Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL

Follow the Specification URL to load the bundle, layer, finding and question structure and the identity and timestamp rules
Follow the Storage type URL to learn the concrete projection in use, whether documents, rows, graph nodes or files, and its canonicalisation rules
Follow the Interface URL to learn the read, create, update and delete operations available and their scopes
Follow the Processes URL for formation, performance, amendment, notice, dispute and disposition procedures
Read the Projection Catalogue URL before emitting anything to a non-party, and the Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL before asserting any legal consequence

coverage.claim: Base claude structure, plus two grok findings, covers agreement identity and legal frame, party positions and authority, formation and execution, agreed text and commercial terms, the obligation/performance/variance lifecycle, and record governance for business-to-business commercial agreements as grounded in the cited instruments. Coverage is asserted only for the sourced instruments and the profiles actually tested; it is not a universal or complete account of commercial contracting, national validity law, or any sector profile, and no conformance to any cited standard is claimed without test evidence.

checklist.notes: Agreement identity, instance boundary and expression addressing are a dedicated finding; party identity uses a governed global identifier; the identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first and excludes dates as identifiers.

Formation, execution, conditional effectiveness, due and performed obligations, breach, remedy, amendment, transfer, termination and post-termination survival each have findings, following the CISG and UNIDROIT division of the contractual life.

Party positions to entities, obligations to source clauses, milestones to obligations, performance to obligations, remedies to breaches and constituent documents to precedence ranks are all modelled; sibling model links are declared as composition.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated; conclusion, dispatch, deemed receipt, execution, effectiveness, due, cure, performance, amendment, termination and disposition times are distinct, with event time separated from observation time.
A dedicated finding applies an agent, activity and derivation vocabulary to every assertion, and derived artifacts such as obligation rule sets carry traceability to source clause identifiers.
Joint ownership by the party positions is a policy and a question; joint facts versus unilateral acts are distinguished, and stewardship and access-grant models are referenced rather than duplicated.

Definiteness of the offer, form requirements, authority verification, signature validation, integrity verification and unfair-term screening are separate validation questions with recorded outcomes and observation times.
Deny-by-default for non-parties, four grant scopes, projection-based disclosure, redaction rules and five enumerated exceptions including adjudication and regulatory access.
Retention triggers, limitation periods, legal holds, the erasure-versus-preservation conflict, redaction in place with preserved digests and evidenced disposition are all modelled.

Alignments are declared with claim levels and mapping conflicts recorded; projections to non-parties are governed artifacts with published omission lists; the model is expressed independently of any storage format.
Subject-matter class, uniform-regime applicability, clause class, party role, notice kind, remedy kind and trade term are all coded against named schemes with versions.
Signing authority basis, limits, verification and the consequences of excess are a dedicated finding, with consent authority for transfers handled separately.
Performance metrics with values, units and thresholds, and quantification of claimed loss against caps or liquidated sums, are explicit questions.
Place of business, named place for the trade term, place of risk transfer, arbitral seat and the offset of the place of execution are captured; geospatial geometry is not required for this model.
Signature assurance, digest fixity, tamper-evident chained audit segments and confidentiality scope are modelled; cryptographic key management is delegated to the trust-service domain.
Authority excess, validity defects, excuse for impediment and hardship, compelled disclosure and erasure conflicts are each modelled as explicit exception paths rather than error states.

known_omissions: Consumer and employment contracts are excluded, so unfair-term regimes specific to consumers are not modelled.
Statutory late-payment interest defaults were not grounded in a verified primary source in this pass; the model carries an interest-basis element but no jurisdictional default table.
Sector-specific master agreement lifecycles, such as derivatives event models, are treated as EXTEND candidates and are not detailed.
Tax determination, customs classification and transfer pricing are out of scope even though they depend on the trade term and price elements.
Escrow, retention of title and security interests are referenced only at their boundary with property transfer, which the uniform sales regime excludes.
Smart-contract execution semantics on distributed ledgers are referenced through the data-sharing essential-requirements source but not modelled as an execution substrate.
Automated clause extraction quality metrics are represented only as a provenance confidence field, with no scoring scheme specified.
Multi-tier supply chain flow-down of terms to subcontracts is acknowledged in the third-party finding but not modelled as a propagation mechanism.
National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, unconscionability, illegality, consideration in common law) lack a uniform primary schema because CISG Article 4 excludes validity.

UCC Article 2 battle of forms (§ 2-207), adequate assurance (§ 2-609) and remedy catalogue were not fetched as live primary text beyond § 2-201; they are regional competitors to CISG, not canonical nodes.

UNIDROIT hardship, set-off, plurality of obligors, assignment chapters and limitation Chapter 10 are aligned from the 2016 instrument as a whole; individual articles beyond formation Chapter 2 were not re-fetched in this run.
The 1974 Limitation Convention (as amended 1980) is a related sales time-bar treaty and is not modelled as a first-class bundle.
Industry standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and clickwrap or platform terms of service are profiles, not core findings.
Smart-contract bytecode, oracles and on-chain settlement have only UNIDROIT automated-contracting comment support and remain an evidence gap.
Supervening sanctions, export controls and COVID-era hardship practice are public-law or factual overlays without a dedicated primary contract schema here.
eIDAS qualified-signature levels and UETA state enactments were not fetched; MLES is the cross-border alignment used instead.
PECL and the Draft Common Frame of Reference were not fetched live and are not treated as canonical.
Data-processing addenda, ESG clauses and modern slavery warranties are emerging clause classes without a governing primary standard in the source set.
conflicts: The uniform sales regime frees contracts of writing and proof requirements, while the New York Convention requires an arbitration agreement in writing: a contract may be validly formed orally yet carry an unenforceable arbitration clause. The model therefore records the writing evidence for the forum clause separately from the formation evidence.

Statutory and contractual retention duties conflict with personal-data erasure rights. The model resolves this by redaction in place with preserved digests, which is a defensible reconciliation rather than a settled legal rule.

Expression-level clause identifiers change when a provision is renumbered by amendment, while work-level identifiers persist. Consumers that key on expression identifiers will break across amendments; the model requires both to be stored.

Hardship and renegotiation exist in the UNIDROIT Principles but have no counterpart in the uniform sales regime, so excuse semantics differ by governing law; the excuse ground code must be interpreted against the declared governing law.
Trade terms allocate cost and risk but not property, and the uniform sales regime expressly excludes the passing of property, so title must be sourced from national law outside this model.
Regional qualified-signature presumptions are not globally comparable with technology-neutral reliability tests, so a single signature assurance level cannot be treated as universally probative.
CISG Article 11 (no writing required) conflicts with UCC § 2-201 (signed writing for $500+) and with CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations that restore a writing rule the parties cannot derogate from.

CISG Article 16 makes offers generally revocable until acceptance is dispatched, with reliance and stated irrevocability exceptions; many civil-law systems treat a fixed-time offer as irrevocable. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.4 comment records this as historically irreconcilable and selects CISG's main rule.

CISG Article 19 material-alteration list is more rigid than UNIDROIT Article 2.1.11 comment, which makes materiality contextual; UCC § 2-207 (unfetched beyond awareness) is a third battle-of-forms regime.
CISG Article 28 lets a court refuse specific performance according to its own law; civil-law systems more readily order performance.
CISG Article 79 impediment is not UNIDROIT hardship; treating force majeure certificates as automatic exemption would be a false conformance claim.
HCCH Article 3 choice of non-State rules of law is commonly allowed in arbitration and often disallowed in State courts unless forum law says otherwise.

Agreed penalties may be unenforceable as penalties in some common-law systems while liquidated damages and civil-law contractual penalties are treated differently; LegalRuleML Penalty is a deontic link, not a guarantee of enforceability.

Akoma Ntoso is designed primarily for parliamentary, legislative and judicial documents; using it for private commercial contracts is an alignment of document mechanics, not a claim that Akoma Ntoso normatively governs private agreements.
regional_assumptions: Electronic signature and trust-service assurance levels and the essential requirements for data-sharing smart contracts are drawn from European Union instruments and are regional alignments, not universal rules.
The Hague choice-of-law principles are non-binding soft law whose adoption varies by jurisdiction; the express-or-tacit choice model may not match a given forum's conflict rules.

The uniform sales regime applies only where the parties' places of business are in contracting states or conflict rules lead there, and it may be excluded by agreement, so its applicability is recorded as a declaration rather than assumed.

Common-law consideration and privity doctrines and civil-law cause requirements differ from the restatement-style formation model used here; formation validity must be re-tested under the declared governing law.
Limitation periods, notice-deeming rules and permitted electronic execution formalities vary by jurisdiction and are treated as configuration rather than as model constants.
International sales between CISG Contracting States default to CISG unless excluded; purely domestic US goods sales more often meet UCC Article 2, including the § 2-201 writing rule.
Rome I Regulation choice-of-law mechanics in the EU were not fetched; HCCH Principles are used as the cross-border alignment and expressly sit alongside Rome I as a non-binding guide.
Article 96 writing reservations (for example historically relevant for some CISG Contracting States) must be checked per party place of business rather than assumed absent.
Islamic finance, OHADA uniform acts and PRC Contract/Civil Code particularities are not included and would be regional extensions.
Places of business, not nationality, determine CISG internationality (CISG Articles 1(3) and 10).
The default operating picture is a B2B commercial agreement, including but not limited to international sales, rather than a consumer, employment or purely domestic consumer-protection regime.
Party-mirror joint ownership is the stewardship default: each party holds a full record and joint facts change only by joint events.
Where CISG and a domestic writing statute both claim to apply, the model records both rules and the Article 96 reservation state rather than silently preferring one.
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever a notice, acceptance or breach declaration is transmitted rather than contemporaneously logged.
Alignment to a standard is not a conformance claim for any particular agreement instance.
adversarial_checks: Tested against oral and conduct-formed contracts: identity must not be derived from a document digest, since no executed document may exist. Agreement identity is therefore separated from expression identity and from execution evidence.

Tested against framework agreements with call-offs: the instance boundary question asks whether obligations arise directly or only on call-off, which prevents a single record silently conflating a master agreement with each purchase under it.

Tested against the battle of forms: the governing text may be a composite of two competing form sets, so incorporation and precedence are modelled independently of the signed instrument rather than assumed from it.
Rejected the framing of a contract as an organization, upholding the registry validation flag: party positions reference organization records, and no organizational attributes are carried here.
Rejected a standalone signature bundle: signature is evidence supporting execution and has no independent decision surface, so it is a finding within formation rather than a top-level concern.

Rejected modelling dispute proceedings, awards and enforcement inline: no cited primary source supports duplicating adjudication process in the contract record, so only the clause, the writing evidence and the escalation state remain in scope.
Rejected owning executed prices as price observations: the valuation model reads a projection, which prevents a confidentiality leak becoming a structural dependency.
Tested whether milestones deserve artifacts: any published schedule can diverge from the clauses that generate it, so schedules are declared derived projections rather than authoritative artifacts.
The registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization is honoured: party positions bind actors; the agreement is a joint record, not an O1 entity.
CISG was not generalised to services, consumer sales, validity or property; those exclusions are modelled as out-of-scope or sibling boundaries.
UNIDROIT PICC were not treated as automatically binding; they apply when chosen, used to interpret or supplement, or selected as HCCH Article 3 rules of law.
Choice of court and arbitration clauses are stored as terms and then handed to the dispute-resolution sibling; HCCH Principles' exclusion of those agreements from choice-of-law scope is respected.
A date is never used as an identifier; execution date is a temporal attribute beside master-system id, IRI and UUID or ULID.
Electronic signature reliability is aligned to MLES rather than inventing a vendor-specific PKI as the semantic model.
Public-summary and credit-standing projections were checked so they cannot leak clause text, prices or personal signatory data by default.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate and both explicitly uphold the registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization. The boundary is the jointly owned multi-party agreement record composed of party positions, clause structure, deontic obligations and lifecycle events, with the legal entities, the procurement award process, adjudication proceedings, proprietary/title effects, insolvency and settlement execution held as neighbouring models. Claude's six sourced boundary notes and grok's CISG/HCCH sphere-of-application notes agree on every exclusion, so the boundary is settled before any node is accepted.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Claude has six sourced boundary notes naming concrete neighbour models, an explicit inline_only_rationale for every finding that mints no artifact, a sixteen-dimension coverage checklist with no self-declared gap, and separate findings for provenance, access, retention and interoperability. Grok is stronger on CISG article-level depth but declares a validation gap and lumps notices, dispute clauses, joint record, access and retention into one composite finding, which is the less clear boundary.

decisions.concept: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
decisions.rationale: A genuine hole in the base: the agreed text can be addressed and ranked but not construed. CISG Articles 7-9 give it primary-source grounding and it duplicates nothing already present.

decisions.concept: Anticipatory breach, suspension, adequate assurance, Nachfrist
decisions.rationale: The base jumps from breach declaration to remedy election with no additional-period, suspension or assurance path. CISG Articles 47, 63, 71-73 support four distinct states the base cannot currently represent.

decisions.concept: Writing requirement, statute of frauds and Article 96 reservations
decisions.disposition: rejected as duplicative; deferred as question-level enrichment
decisions.rationale: The base finding execution-signature-and-form already owns the form-requirement decision surface. Adding grok's finding would create a second execution node overlapping on signature method. The CISG Article 11 versus UCC 2-201 versus Article 12/96 tension is recorded as a publication hold and deferred research item instead of new structure.

decisions.concept: Remedy catalogue detail (mitigation, substitute-transaction measure, Article 28 forum filter, restitution)
decisions.rationale: Base breach-excuse-and-remedy already carries remedy election and quantification against caps or liquidated sums, and termination-expiry-and-survival carries wind-down and final accounting. Grok's additions are measurement refinements inside an existing surface, not a missing surface.

decisions.concept: Composite notices/dispute-clause/joint-record/access/retention finding
decisions.disposition: rejected in favour of base decomposition
decisions.rationale: The base already separates notice-and-formal-communication, dispute-forum-and-enforceability, access-and-disclosure-control, retention-limitation-and-deletion and provenance-and-audit-trail. Importing a composite would blur four distinct governance decision surfaces the base keeps apart.

decisions.concept: Assignment, guarantees and third-party rights as one node
decisions.rationale: The base splits this correctly into third-party-positions (agents, guarantors, beneficiaries, subcontracting) and assignment-and-novation (transfer kind, consent, change of control, position continuity). Grok's single node would double-own both.

decisions.concept: Clause isomorphism and standard-versus-negotiated flag
decisions.rationale: Base cla-q-machine-rule-link covers the rule-to-provision assertion and oac-q-standard-terms covers incorporation of competing form sets. Many-to-many isomorphism is a refinement of an existing question, not a new finding.

decisions.concept: Delivery, conformity, examination and seller cure
decisions.rationale: Base delivery-and-risk-transfer holds conformity and examination periods, performance-record-and-acceptance holds acceptance and rejection states, and milestone-and-due-condition holds cure periods. Grok's node restates all three.

decisions.concept: Risk passing, impediment and hardship
decisions.rationale: Base del-q-risk-transfer covers the passing of risk and brm-q-excuse-ground covers impediment and hardship with evidence. CISG Article 80 self-caused failure is a worthwhile question-level addition but does not justify a parallel finding.

decisions.concept: Statutory default duties not created by a clause (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59)
decisions.rationale: Base obl-q-source-clause presumes a provision creates each duty, so gap-filled statutory duties currently have no source. This is a real modelling question about whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, and it needs its own resolution rather than an imported node.

decisions.concept: Artifact discipline via inline_only_rationale
decisions.rationale: The base refuses to mint artifacts for derived readings of clause text (payment terms, protective terms, milestones, termination state) to prevent a second normatively significant copy of the executed wording. This discipline is preserved and grok's flatter artifact set is not merged.

decisions.concept: Incoterms trade terms and risk-transfer point
decisions.rationale: Grok has no trade-term source at all; the base grounds delivery, cost allocation and the named place in ICC Incoterms 2020, which is required for any goods-sale profile.

decisions.concept: eIDAS and Data Act sourced elements
decisions.rationale: Signature assurance levels, trust-service concepts and unfair-term controls in the base come from EU instruments. They stay, marked as regional alignment rather than universal rule, consistent with grok's use of the UNCITRAL model laws as the cross-border baseline.

decisions.concept: National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, illegality)
decisions.rationale: CISG Article 4 excludes validity and both providers place it in a sibling or overlay. The base keeps only the assertion surface in effectiveness-conditions-and-validity, which is the correct minimum without importing grok's declared validation gap.

publicationHolds: Source verification hold: none of the 16 base URLs or the 5 grok-only URLs were re-fetched in this adjudication. Every accepted source must be resolved live and version-pinned before publication, with particular attention to the two different LegalRuleML OS URLs, Akoma Ntoso naming-convention v1.0 versus core v1.0 Part 1, UBL 2.4 Committee Specification status, Incoterms 2020, and eIDAS 'as amended by the European Digital Identity framework'.

Multi-profile validation hold: the merged structure must be exercised against at least three domain profiles before publication - an international CISG sale of goods, a domestic US goods sale where UCC Article 2 and the section 2-201 writing rule apply, and a services or framework-plus-call-off agreement where no goods and no executed single instrument exist.

Writing-rule hold: CISG Article 11 (no writing required), CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations, and UCC section 2-201 must be carried as co-recorded competing rules with the reservation state per party place of business. Do not publish a single resolved writing rule.

Regional-labelling hold: eIDAS signature assurance levels and the Data Act unfair-term and smart-contract essential-requirement material are EU-regional and must be published as regional alignments, not universal rules, alongside the technology-neutral UNCITRAL reliability test.

No-conformance hold: alignments to UBL, LegalRuleML, Akoma Ntoso, PROV-O and RFC 3339 are declared alignments only. Publication must state the claim level and must not assert tested conformance for any instance without test evidence.
deferredResearch: Fetch UCC Article 2 primary text beyond section 2-201 - specifically 2-207 battle of forms, 2-609 adequate assurance, and the 2-706/2-708/2-712/2-713 damages measures - to test whether the accepted anticipatory-breach finding holds under a second, non-CISG regime.

Resolve whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, so that gap-filled statutory duties (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59) can be instantiated without a fabricated provision reference.
Ground statutory late-payment interest defaults in a verified primary source, or publish the interest-basis element explicitly as configuration with no jurisdictional default table.
Assess the 1974 UN Limitation Convention as amended in 1980 as a distinct time-bar instrument against the base retention and limitation-period questions.
Evaluate sector standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and insurance policies as EXTEND profiles, and confirm the base carries the extension points those profiles would need.

Compare eIDAS qualified-signature presumptions, UETA/ESIGN state enactments and the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures reliability test to determine whether a single cross-regional signature assurance scale is defensible.

Decide whether set-off, plurality of obligors and transfer of obligations (UNIDROIT Chapters 8, 9, 11) belong in the accepted transfer surface or in a sibling model, since neither provider currently owns set-off.
Specify the smart-contract execution substrate boundary: whether self-executing performance is evidence of performance only, or requires its own recorded execution state.

model.name: Observation / Measurement Record
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral context structure for a single observation act and the measurement record it produces, binding a feature of interest, an observable property, an observing procedure, a result value and its unit, together with time, uncertainty, quality, provenance and governance context, so that an AI agent can create, inspect, validate and operate observation records without owning the lifecycles of the sensors, samples, methods or catalogues it references.
model.scope_statement: The subject is the observation event and its resulting record: the act of determining a value for an observable property of a feature of interest by applying an observing procedure, plus everything needed to interpret, trust, correlate and retire that single record. OMS/ISO 19156 and SOSA/SSN both model an Observation as an execution (an act), so this model is an event, not the sensor, the sample, the property definition or the dataset. It carries references, bindings and observation-specific parameters for those neighbours; it does not reproduce their identity, lifecycle or operational machinery. Storage and interface (JSON, XML, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB, relational LIMS tables) are projections of this semantics, never part of it.
in_scope: Identity, versioning and classification of one observation record and of the observation act it documents
Binding to exactly one observable property and one observing procedure, and to the observer, host and deployment that executed it, by reference
Proximate and ultimate feature of interest, and the reference to the sample or sampling chain when observation is indirect
Result representation: value, datatype, cardinality, complex or coverage payloads, and the unit of measure or quantity-kind binding
Absent, censored, below-detection-limit, out-of-range and non-numeric results, with the reason they are absent or bounded
Measurement uncertainty statements (standard, expanded, coverage factor and coverage probability) recorded against the result
References to metrological traceability chains and calibration evidence held by other models
Reference ranges, interpretation codes and recorded statements of conformity together with the identifier of the decision rule applied
Temporal frame: phenomenon time, result time, valid time and ingestion or observation-capture time, each with explicit offsets
Aggregation duration, interpolation type, cumulative flags and sampling regime that determine how the value may be resampled
Observation geometry, observed area and the environmental or operating conditions in force during the act
Record lifecycle status, amendment, correction, supersession and retraction semantics for this record only
Recorded quality flags and quality-control outcomes produced elsewhere, plus references to the evidence supporting them
Provenance chain, derivation from prior observations, responsible agents, ownership and attribution
Access classification, retention binding, and identifier resolution and cross-system correlation
Alignment declarations and encoding bindings to external observation standards, and membership in collections, datastreams or series
out_of_scope: The sensor, instrument or observing system as a managed asset, including its own registration, maintenance, firmware and decommissioning lifecycle
Calibration and traceability records as governed documents: this model references a calibration certificate but does not issue, renew, revoke or verify one
The sample or specimen as an entity, including collection, preparation, custody transfer, storage and disposal lifecycle
Definition and governance of observable properties, quantity kinds and controlled vocabularies, including term proposal, deprecation and mapping maintenance
Unit-of-measure registry maintenance, unit conversion tables and dimensional-analysis services
The observing procedure or test method as a controlled specification, including method development, validation studies and version approval
Execution of quality-control tests, rule evaluation, thresholding or automated flagging: this model records the outcome and its provenance, never the evaluator
Audit-trail capture, tamper-evidence infrastructure and electronic-signature enforcement, which belong to the electronic-records model
Physical execution of deletion, purge or anonymisation; this model records the disposition decision and its policy binding only
Dataset catalogue publication, licensing negotiation, DOI minting and distribution management for collections of observations
Downstream analytics, model assimilation, forecasting and statistical inference beyond recording that a result was derived
Sensor tasking, actuation and control commands
Laboratory quality-management-system scope, accreditation status and personnel competence records
Transport-level streaming guarantees, message ordering, delivery semantics and API pagination

boundary_notes.distinction: OMS and SOSA separate the Sample (a feature used to represent another feature) from the Observation (the act). This model carries the reference from the observation to its proximate feature of interest and, where that is a sample, to the sample identifier and the ultimate feature it stands for. Sample identity, sampling act, preparation steps, sub-sampling relationships and custody remain owned by the sample model.

OMS requires an observation to name exactly one ObservableProperty, and QUDT separates QuantityKind from Unit. This model holds the reference and any observation-specific constraint or qualifier on the measurand; it does not define the property term, its dimension, its synonyms or its deprecation policy.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Unit of Measure Registry (UCUM / SI / QUDT)
boundary_notes.distinction: UCUM and QUDT are governed unit code systems. This model records which code system and code express the result, and any observation-level scaling; it never redefines units, conversion multipliers or dimensional vectors, and it must not silently convert values.

SOSA defines Procedure as a workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm or computational method, and OMS makes the ObservingProcedure a first-class feature. This model records which procedure version was executed and the execution-specific parameters; method authoring, validation and approval belong to the method model.

OMS models Observer, Host and Deployment (with deploymentReason and deploymentTime) as separate features. This model references the observer and the deployment in force at the time of the act; asset lifecycle, platform management and deployment scheduling stay outside.

VIM defines metrological traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations. This model records the traceability declaration and pointers to the calibration evidence in force; it does not model the calibration act, the reference standard hierarchy or accreditation validity.

QARTOD publishes QC test procedures and flag conventions; SensorThings exposes resultQuality as a recorded property. This model stores the resulting flag, the identifier of the test and the identifier of the evaluating agent. Rule authoring, threshold configuration, execution and re-evaluation are owned by the quality-control model and never by this one.

MHRA GxP data-integrity expectations place audit trail, tamper-evidence and signature control on the records system. This model requires that a record be linkable to its audit entries and preserves the original acquisition record as an artifact, but it does not define, generate, secure or query the audit trail itself.

DCAT governs Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService, with licensing, access rights and versioning at dataset level. This model records membership pointers from an observation to the collection, datastream or series that contains it; catalogue-level metadata, distribution management and publication workflow stay in the catalogue model.

SensorThings binds unitOfMeasurement and observationType at Datastream level, and the OGC Timeseries Profile defines series-level defaults such as interpolationType. Series-level defaults are referenced here so a single record remains interpretable in isolation, but the series aggregate owns its own identity, extent, default resolution and completeness accounting.

This model records which retention policy applies, the disposition decision and the tombstone it leaves behind. Policy authoring, legal-hold determination and the physical execution of destruction are owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy.

sources.title: Observations, Measurements, and Samples (OMS)
sources.version_or_date: OMS version 3.0, OGC Abstract Specification Topic 20 (OGC 20-082r4), published jointly as ISO 19156:2023
sources.relevance: Defines the normative conceptual schema for observations, for the features involved in the observation process and for sampling features, including sample typing by spatial, material and statistical nature and relationships between samples. Anchors the scope and top-level structure of this model.

sources.title: OMS Abstract Specification feature catalogue input (opengeospatial/om-swg)
sources.organization: Open Geospatial Consortium (OMS Standards Working Group)
sources.version_or_date: Working feature catalogue, draft status, dated 2021-08-20 in the document header
sources.relevance: Working OGC material listing the OMS classes and their properties: Observation (phenomenonTime, resultTime, validTime, resultQuality, parameter, observedProperty, observer, observingProcedure, proximate and ultimate featureOfInterest, result, relatedObservation), ObservableProperty, Observer, ObservingProcedure, Deployment (deploymentReason, deploymentTime, host), Sample (sampleType, sampledFeature, sampling, preparationStep, relatedSample) and Host. Explicitly working-draft; multiplicities must be re-verified against the published standard.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SOSA/SSN), 2023 Edition
sources.version_or_date: 2023 Edition; namespace http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/, version IRI http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/2023/; document state as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: Provides the lightweight core vocabulary for Observation, Sample, Sampling, Sampler, FeatureOfInterest, ObservableProperty, Procedure, Platform, System and Deployment, with hasResult, hasSimpleResult, resultTime, phenomenonTime, madeBySensor, usedProcedure, isSampleOf and hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest, plus the system-capability and operating-conditions module used for context of applicability.

sources.title: OGC SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing, Version 1.1 (OGC 18-088)
sources.relevance: Concrete normative realisation of the observation model with Thing, Location, HistoricalLocation, Datastream, Sensor, ObservedProperty, Observation and FeatureOfInterest. Supplies Observation properties phenomenonTime, result, resultTime, resultQuality, validTime and parameters, and the Datastream-level unitOfMeasurement, observationType and observedArea used to justify series-level versus record-level binding.

sources.title: OGC Timeseries Profile of Observations and Measurements (OGC 15-043r3)
sources.relevance: Establishes that correct machine interpretation of a value requires interpolation type, point versus interval or accumulation semantics, aggregation duration, cumulative flags, qualifiers, censored reason and nil-reason handling, plus series-level defaults. Grounds the aggregation, interpolation and censoring findings.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the provenance vocabulary used as an alignment: Entity, Activity and Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime and endedAtTime, plus the qualified pattern (Generation, Derivation, Attribution, Association, Usage) for recording responsibility and derivation of an observation.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile requiring an explicit stated offset to UTC (Z or numeric offset), defining seconds and optional fractional seconds, the -00:00 convention for an unknown local offset, leap-second handling and the conditions under which timestamps sort as strings. Governs every temporal value in this model.

sources.title: JCGM Publications: Guides in Metrology (JCGM 100:2008 GUM; JCGM 200:2012 VIM; JCGM 106:2012; JCGM GUM-6:2020)
sources.organization: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures / Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
sources.version_or_date: JCGM 100:2008 (with Amd.1:2026), JCGM 101:2008, JCGM 102:2011, JCGM 106:2012, JCGM 200:2012, JCGM GUM-1:2023, JCGM GUM-6:2020; publications page as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: Authoritative vocabulary and method for measurand, measurement result, measured quantity value, standard and expanded measurement uncertainty, coverage interval and coverage probability, metrological traceability, calibration, measurement procedure, influence quantity, detection limit, trueness and precision, and for the role of measurement uncertainty in conformity assessment.

sources.title: The Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM) Specification
sources.organization: Regenstrief Institute, Inc. and the UCUM Organization
sources.relevance: Machine-oriented unit code system built for electronic data interchange, with case-sensitive and case-insensitive symbol forms over 7-bit US-ASCII and compound expressions with multiplication and division operators. Used as the default unit-code binding and as evidence that a unit binding must name its code system.

sources.title: QUDT Ontologies (Quantities, Units, Dimensions and Data Types)
sources.relevance: Separates QuantityKind, Unit, Quantity, QuantityValue, Dimension Vector and System of Units, with conversion multipliers and offsets and applicable-unit relations. Justifies modelling quantity kind and unit as two distinct bindings rather than a single free-text unit string.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Observation resource
sources.relevance: An independent, widely deployed observation model used as an alignment and counterexample source: identifier, status (registered, preliminary, final, amended), category, code (1..1), subject, focus, effective[x], issued, performer, value[x], dataAbsentReason, interpretation, method, specimen, device, referenceRange, hasMember, derivedFrom and component. Grounds record status, absent-reason, interpretation, composite results and member relationships.

sources.title: ILAC Guidance Series (ILAC-G8:09/2019 Guidelines on Decision Rules and Statements of Conformity; ILAC-G17:01/2021 ILAC Guidelines for Measurement Uncertainty in Testing)
sources.relevance: Normative accreditation guidance requiring that a statement of conformity identify the results it applies to, the specification met or not met, and the decision rule applied, and requiring documented evaluation and reporting of measurement uncertainty under ISO/IEC 17025:2017. Grounds the conformity and uncertainty findings.

sources.title: 'GXP' Data Integrity Guidance and Definitions
sources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
sources.version_or_date: Published 9 March 2018; last updated 27 September 2021; notes that the OECD Advisory Document on Data Integrity (September 2021) takes precedence for GLP facilities
sources.relevance: Regulator statement of data-integrity expectations across the regulated lifecycle, covering original records and true copies, contemporaneous capture, audit trail, and retention and archiving. Grounds the original-acquisition-record artifact, the amendment rules and the retention and disposition finding, while leaving audit-trail machinery to the records system.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Defines Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService with temporal and spatial coverage, prov:wasGeneratedBy, dcat:qualifiedRelation, versioning (hasVersion, previousVersion), dcterms:accessRights, license and identifier. Used to place catalogue-level publication, licensing and versioning outside this model while retaining membership and access-rights references.

sources.title: QARTOD - Quality Assurance / Quality Control of Real Time Oceanographic Data
sources.organization: NOAA U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System (IOOS)
sources.version_or_date: Programme active since 2003; Manual for Oceanographic Data Quality Control Flags version 1.2 final; manuals for 14 core variables described as living documents
sources.relevance: Public-authority evidence that quality flags are a distinct, documented, test-driven layer over a value: primary flags (pass, not evaluated, suspect, fail, missing), separate real-time and delayed-mode regimes, and per-variable test manuals. Grounds the quality-flag finding and the separation of flag recording from flag evaluation.

sources.title: WIGOS Metadata Guidelines for Data Providers (wmo-im/et-acdm wiki, referencing WMO-No. 1192 and schemas.wmo.int/wmdr)
sources.organization: World Meteorological Organization (Expert Team on Metadata, Information Management)
sources.version_or_date: WMO-No. 1192 WIGOS Metadata Standard cited as the published standard; wiki page as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: First-party WMO working guidance confirming that observational metadata is organised into categories covering station and facility characteristics, deployments and instruments with begin and end dates, data quality and processing, ownership and data policy, and contacts, and that different organisations are the authoritative source for different categories. Used for the ownership, environment and data-policy findings; the standard text itself was not read and this is recorded as an evidence gap.

bundles.name: Observation Act and Identity
bundles.description: Establishes what one observation record is: how it is identified and versioned, how it is classified, and how it binds to the procedure execution and the executing observer that produced it.
bundles.rationale: OMS and SOSA both define an Observation as the execution of an observing procedure, not as a value. Any agent operating on such records must first resolve identity, kind and the act itself before it can interpret anything else; SensorThings and FHIR both make identity and a typed classification mandatory entry points.

layers.name: Record Identity and Kind
layers.description: Identity, versioning and classification of the observation record and of the act it documents.

findings.name: Observation record identity and version identity
findings.description: How a single observation record is uniquely and stably identified, how the identity of the record is distinguished from the identity of the observation act, and how successive versions of the same record are identified without colliding with new observations.

questions.text: Which system is the master system of record for this observation, and what identifier does it issue?
answer_data: Issuing system identifier and its role (LIMS, SCADA historian, observing service, clinical system)
Whether the identifier is guaranteed stable across export and re-import

questions.text: Is this identifier for the observation act or for the record that documents it, and how are the two related when one act yields several records?
answer_data: Relationship statement between act and record
Count of records documenting the same act

questions.text: How is a corrected or reprocessed version of this record identified relative to its predecessor?
answer_data: Whether the base identifier is retained across versions
Rule stating that a new version never reuses a superseded version identifier

questions.text: If no authoritative or governed identifier exists, what surrogate is minted and how is that fact recorded?
answer_data: Minting authority within the adopting Dimension
Flag marking the identifier as surrogate
Migration rule for when an authoritative identifier later appears

data_elements.name: observationIdentifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the observation record, resolved under the model identity priority.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Name or IRI of the scheme, namespace or issuing authority that governs the primary identifier.

data_elements.name: alternateIdentifier
data_elements.description: Business or legacy identifiers carried alongside the primary identifier, each qualified by its scheme.

data_elements.name: recordVersion
data_elements.description: Version designator of this record, monotonic within the base identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data: a set of identifier values, their schemes and their version relations. It has no rendered or stored form of its own, and materialising it as a document would create a second, competing source of truth against the master system that issues the identifier.

findings.name: Observation kind and result-type classification
findings.description: How an observation is typed so that an agent can predict the shape of the result and the applicable interpretation rules: the observation type or result type, the domain category, and whether the observation is direct, derived, simulated or estimated.

questions.text: What result type does this observation declare, and does the declared type match the actual result payload?
answer_data: Observation or result type code (measure, count, category, truth, complex, coverage, timeseries)

questions.text: Under which domain category or programme is this observation classified for discovery and rule selection?
Was the value obtained by direct determination, by derivation from other observations, by simulation or by expert estimation?
answer_data: Reference to source observations where derived
Justification note for estimated or simulated values

questions.text: Which observation profile or requirements class does this record claim to satisfy?
answer_data: Whether conformance was tested or only asserted

data_elements.name: observationType
data_elements.description: Code declaring the type of the result, controlling how the result payload is interpreted.

data_elements.name: domainCategory
data_elements.description: Domain or programme classification of the observation, drawn from a named vocabulary.

data_elements.name: determinationMode
data_elements.description: Whether the value was directly determined, derived, simulated or estimated.

data_elements.name: claimedProfile
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the observation profile the record asserts conformance to, with an explicit tested-or-asserted marker.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification consists of coded values drawn from external vocabularies plus a profile reference. The code lists themselves are owned by vocabulary and profile registries, so this finding carries codes and references only and produces no artifact of its own.

layers.name: Act and Procedure Execution
layers.description: The binding between the observation record and the procedure, observer, host and deployment that executed it, together with the execution-specific parameters in force.

findings.name: Procedure, observer, host and deployment binding
findings.description: How the record names the observing procedure that was executed, the observer or system that executed it, the host or platform carrying that observer, and the deployment in force at the time, each by reference to the model that owns it.

questions.text: Which observing procedure, at which version, was executed to produce this result?
answer_data: Procedure model or registry that owns the reference
Whether the executed version is still current

questions.text: Which observer, sensor, analyst or computational system carried out the procedure?
answer_data: Reference to the asset model entry, if any

questions.text: Which deployment of that observer onto which host was in force when the act occurred?
answer_data: Deployment time interval covering the act
Deployment reason recorded by the owning model

questions.text: Were there documented deviations from the procedure during this execution, and where is the deviation record held?
answer_data: Reference to the deviation or nonconformance record

data_elements.name: observingProcedureRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the procedure specification and version executed for this observation.

data_elements.name: observerRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the observer, sensor, analyst or computational system that executed the procedure.

data_elements.name: deploymentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the deployment of the observer on a host that was in force at the time of the act.

data_elements.name: procedureDeviation
data_elements.description: Recorded deviation from the procedure during this execution, with a pointer to the owning deviation record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Every element here is an outbound reference to a procedure, asset or deviation record owned by a sibling model. Reproducing those objects locally would duplicate their lifecycles; the record therefore stores only the reference, the version pinned at execution time and the deviation pointer.

findings.name: Observation parameters and influence quantities
findings.description: Named execution parameters and influence quantities that qualify the observation but are neither the measurand nor the result: settings, conditions applied, dilution or scaling factors, and any parameter needed to make the result reproducible.

questions.text: Which named parameters qualify this observation, and what value and unit does each carry?
answer_data: Parameter name and defining vocabulary reference
Parameter unit code and code system
Whether the parameter is mandatory for the declared procedure

questions.text: Which influence quantities were recorded or controlled because they affect the measured value?
answer_data: Whether it was measured, controlled or assumed
Reference to the correction applied, if any

questions.text: Which parameters are inherited from the series, datastream or method default rather than stated on this record?
answer_data: Source of the default (series, datastream, method)

data_elements.name: observationParameter
data_elements.description: Named value qualifying the observation act, each with name, value, optional unit and defining vocabulary reference.

data_elements.name: influenceQuantity
data_elements.description: Quantity that is not the measurand but affects the relation between indication and result, with its recorded value and control status.

data_elements.name: parameterInheritance
data_elements.description: Statement of which effective parameters were inherited from a series or method default and which were overridden on this record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameters are name-value-unit triples plus an inheritance statement. They are read and written as structured fields on the record, and the vocabularies that define parameter names belong to the property registry, so no separate artifact is warranted.

bundles.name: Subject and Property Binding
bundles.description: What was observed and on what: the feature of interest chain including any sample that stood in for it, and the observable property and measurand actually determined.
bundles.rationale: OMS requires an observation to name its feature of interest and exactly one observable property, and distinguishes the proximate feature (often a sample) from the ultimate feature the result is about. Misbinding either makes the result uninterpretable, so these are separated from the result itself.

layers.name: Feature of Interest Chain
layers.description: The proximate and ultimate features of interest and the sampling chain that connects them.

findings.name: Proximate and ultimate feature of interest
findings.description: How the record states the feature the result is actually about and, where observation was indirect, the intermediate feature that was directly observed, so that a result taken on a sample is never mistaken for a result taken on the whole.

questions.text: Which real-world feature is this result ultimately a statement about?
Which feature was directly observed, and does it differ from the ultimate feature?
answer_data: Indicator of whether proximate and ultimate differ
Kind of stand-in (sample, sampling location, proxy feature)

questions.text: On what basis is the proximate feature held to represent the ultimate feature, and what limits that representativeness?
answer_data: Reference to the sampling design or plan

questions.text: How is a feature reference resolved when the referenced feature is renamed, merged or split?

data_elements.name: ultimateFeatureOfInterestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the feature the observation result is ultimately about.

data_elements.name: proximateFeatureOfInterestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the feature that was directly observed, where different from the ultimate feature.

data_elements.name: representativenessBasis
data_elements.description: Statement of the basis on which the proximate feature represents the ultimate feature, with known limits.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding carries two typed references and a short justification statement. Feature entities, their geometry and their naming history are owned by the entity models being referenced, so materialising them here would duplicate another model's records.

findings.name: Sample linkage and sampling-chain reference
findings.description: How an observation made on a sample records which sample, where that sample sits in a sub-sampling or derivation chain, and which preparation steps had been applied before the observation, without absorbing the sample lifecycle.

questions.text: Which sample or specimen was this observation performed on?
answer_data: Reference to the sample model entry

questions.text: Where does that sample sit in the sub-sampling or derived-sample chain relative to the originally collected sample?
Which preparation steps had been applied to the sample at the moment of observation?
answer_data: Preparation step references in applied order
Preparation completion state at observation time

questions.text: Were there sample-condition findings that qualify the validity of this result?
answer_data: Sample condition code (for example haemolysed, degraded, contaminated, out of hold time)

data_elements.name: sampleRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the sample or specimen on which the observation was performed.

data_elements.name: samplingChainRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the parent sample and the relationship kind connecting it to the observed sample.

data_elements.name: preparationStateAtObservation
data_elements.description: Ordered references to the preparation steps completed on the sample before this observation.

data_elements.name: sampleConditionCode
data_elements.description: Coded condition of the sample that qualifies result validity, with a pointer to the owning condition record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The sample, its collection act, its preparation steps and its custody are owned by the sample model. This finding exists to pin the exact sample state that applied at observation time, expressed entirely as references and coded qualifiers, so it must not carry sample artifacts.

layers.name: Observable Property and Measurand
layers.description: The property observed and the fully qualified measurand, including the conditions that make the quantity intended to be measured unambiguous.

findings.name: Observable property binding
findings.description: How the record names exactly one observable property by reference to a governed vocabulary, distinguishes the property from its quantity kind, and handles properties that are only definable relative to a method.

questions.text: Which observable property term, from which governed vocabulary and version, does this observation determine?
What quantity kind underlies the property, and is it dimensionally consistent with the recorded unit?
answer_data: Consistency verdict against the recorded unit

questions.text: Is this property method-defined such that results from different procedures are not comparable?
answer_data: Procedure reference that defines the property

questions.text: Is the observed characteristic a quantity or a nominal property with no magnitude?
answer_data: Code list reference for nominal values
Consequence for unit and uncertainty requirements

data_elements.name: observedPropertyRef
data_elements.description: Reference to exactly one governed observable property term determined by this observation.

data_elements.name: quantityKindRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the quantity kind underlying the property, used for dimensional validation.

data_elements.name: methodDefinedProperty
data_elements.description: Indicator that the property is defined by its measurement procedure and is not comparable across procedures.

data_elements.name: propertyNature
data_elements.description: Whether the characteristic is a quantity or a nominal property without magnitude.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The property term, its label, its dimension and its governance all live in the vocabulary registry. This finding contributes only the pinned reference, the derived quantity-kind link and two discriminating flags, which are structured fields rather than a document.

findings.name: Measurand specification and stated conditions
findings.description: The quantity intended to be measured, stated completely enough to be unambiguous: the property, the feature or matrix it is measured in, and the conditions (temperature, pressure, basis, fraction, time base) under which it is defined.

questions.text: What is the complete statement of the quantity intended to be measured, including the conditions that define it?
answer_data: Measurand statement text or structured expression
Defining conditions with values and units

questions.text: On what basis is the value expressed (wet or dry, as-received, normalised, per unit mass, volume or area)?
answer_data: Whether the basis is a series-level default

questions.text: What definitional uncertainty arises because the measurand is not fully specified, and is it bounded?
answer_data: Whether it is included in the reported uncertainty

questions.text: Over what time base or integration window is the measurand defined?
answer_data: Whether it is instantaneous, averaged or accumulated

data_elements.name: measurandStatement
data_elements.description: Complete statement of the quantity intended to be measured with its defining conditions.

data_elements.name: expressionBasis
data_elements.description: Coded basis on which the value is expressed, including any normalisation reference.

data_elements.name: definitionalUncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty arising from incomplete specification of the measurand, with an indicator of whether it is included in the reported uncertainty.

data_elements.name: measurandTimeBase
data_elements.description: Integration window or time base over which the measurand is defined.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The measurand specification is a compact structured statement attached to the record. Where a fuller specification exists it belongs to the method document owned by the procedure model, so this finding deliberately holds the statement and its conditions inline rather than duplicating a method artifact.

bundles.name: Result, Quantity and Uncertainty
bundles.description: The result itself: its value and datatype, its unit and quantity binding, its absence or censoring, the uncertainty attached to it, the traceability that makes it comparable, and the interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SensorThings and FHIR all model the result as a typed slot that can hold simple, complex or absent values, while VIM and GUM require a measurement result to consist of a measured value together with information about its uncertainty. Separating value, unit, absence, uncertainty, traceability and interpretation prevents the common failure of storing a bare number.

layers.name: Result Representation
layers.description: How the result value is represented, dimensioned and qualified when it is missing or bounded.

findings.name: Result value, datatype and cardinality
findings.description: How the result payload is carried for simple scalars, categorical values, vectors, components, coverages, images and time-series blocks, including how the declared datatype constrains the payload and how multi-component results relate to their parent.

questions.text: What is the shape of the result payload, and which datatype governs its parsing?
answer_data: Payload shape (scalar, category, vector, component set, coverage, series block, binary object)
Encoding declaration for binary or structured payloads

questions.text: If the result has components, what is each component's property, value and unit, and can the parent be interpreted without them?
answer_data: Component list with property reference, value and unit
Component ordering rule where order is significant

questions.text: How many significant figures or what resolution does the recorded value carry, and is that a property of the value or of its rendering?
answer_data: Statement separating stored precision from display rounding

questions.text: For a large or binary result payload, how is the payload bound to the record and its integrity verified?

data_elements.name: resultValue
data_elements.description: The value determined by the observation, typed according to the declared observation type.

data_elements.name: resultDatatype
data_elements.description: Identifier of the datatype governing parsing of the result payload.

data_elements.name: resultComponent
data_elements.description: Component of a composite result, each with its own property reference, value and unit.

data_elements.name: recordedResolution
data_elements.description: Resolution or number of significant figures actually carried by the stored value, distinct from display rounding.

artifacts.name: Result payload object
artifacts.description: The stored payload of a complex or binary result that cannot be expressed as a scalar field: spectra, chromatograms, waveforms, images, point clouds, coverage grids or serialised time-series blocks. The payload is bound to the observation record by reference and digest, and is treated as read-only once the record leaves draft.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the payload locator issued by the storing system, qualified by the parent observation identifier and a zero-based part index where a result is split into ordered parts; a content digest is recorded so that identity can be re-established independently of the locator.

findings.name: Unit of measure and quantity binding
findings.description: How the unit of a quantitative result is recorded unambiguously by naming both the code system and the code, how series-level unit defaults are reconciled with record-level values, and why conversion is forbidden without recording it.

questions.text: Which unit code, from which unit code system and version, applies to the recorded value?
answer_data: Unit code system name and version (for example UCUM, QUDT, SI symbol set)
Case sensitivity form used where the code system distinguishes forms

questions.text: If the series or datastream declares a unit and this record declares another, which prevails and how is the conflict recorded?
Was the value converted from the unit in which it was originally determined, and where is that conversion recorded?
answer_data: Agent or system performing the conversion

questions.text: If no unit is recorded, is the result genuinely dimensionless or non-quantitative, and how is that asserted?
answer_data: Validation verdict rejecting silently missing units on quantities

data_elements.name: unitCode
data_elements.description: Unit code applied to the result value.

data_elements.name: unitCodeSystem
data_elements.description: Name and version of the unit code system that governs the unit code.

data_elements.name: unitBindingSource
data_elements.description: Whether the effective unit came from this record or was inherited from a series or datastream declaration, with the precedence rule applied.

data_elements.name: unitConversionRecord
data_elements.description: Record of any conversion from the originally determined unit, holding original value, original unit, factor, offset, rounding and responsible agent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit binding is a pair of coded references plus a conversion audit stub. The unit definitions, conversion multipliers and dimensional vectors are owned by the unit registry, and duplicating them locally would risk drift from the governed code system.

findings.name: Absent, censored and bounded results
findings.description: How the record expresses that no value exists, that a value is bounded rather than determined (below detection or quantitation limit, above range), or that a value was suppressed, so that absence is never encoded as zero or as an unexplained null.

questions.text: If no result value is present, what is the declared reason for its absence?
answer_data: Absence reason code (not performed, not applicable, error, withheld, lost, out of hold time)
Free-text explanation where the code is insufficient
