questions.text: Is the value censored, and if so what is the bound, its direction and the limit that produced it?
answer_data: Limit kind (detection limit, quantitation limit, instrument range)
Reference to how the limit was established

questions.text: What rule must a consumer apply when aggregating or comparing a censored value?
answer_data: Substitution policy if any and its owner

questions.text: If the value exists but is withheld, what authority withheld it and under what condition may it be released?

data_elements.name: dataAbsentReason
data_elements.description: Coded reason a result value is absent from the record.

data_elements.name: censoring
data_elements.description: Censoring statement holding direction, bound value, unit and the kind of limit that produced the bound.

data_elements.name: detectionLimitRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the established detection or quantitation limit applicable to this procedure and matrix.

data_elements.name: suppressionMarker
data_elements.description: Marker that an existing value is withheld, with the withholding authority reference and release condition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Absence and censoring are expressed as coded reasons, bounds and references to limits established by the method model. There is nothing to render or store as a separate object, and creating one would encourage treating a censored value as though it were a determined value.

layers.name: Uncertainty, Traceability and Interpretation
layers.description: What makes the result usable as evidence: its stated uncertainty, its metrological traceability, and any interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty statement
findings.description: How the uncertainty associated with the reported value is stated so that it can be used: the kind of uncertainty, its value and unit, the coverage factor and coverage probability where expanded, and the basis on which it was evaluated.

questions.text: What kind of uncertainty is reported, with what numeric value and unit?
answer_data: Uncertainty kind (standard, combined standard, expanded, coverage interval)
Uncertainty value and unit or relative expression
Whether it is absolute or relative to the result

questions.text: For an expanded uncertainty, what coverage factor and coverage probability apply?
answer_data: Assumed distribution or effective degrees of freedom

questions.text: On what basis was the uncertainty evaluated, and which uncertainty budget or method does it come from?
answer_data: Evaluation basis (measurement model, validation data, proficiency testing, control chart)
Reference to the uncertainty budget owned by the method model
Whether contributions specific to this observation were added

questions.text: If no uncertainty is reported, is that a declared decision and on what ground?
answer_data: Ground for omission (not relevant to validity, not required for this result type)

data_elements.name: uncertaintyKind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of the reported uncertainty.

data_elements.name: uncertaintyValue
data_elements.description: Numeric uncertainty with its unit or relative expression.

data_elements.name: coverageParameters
data_elements.description: Coverage factor, coverage probability and assumed distribution or effective degrees of freedom for an expanded uncertainty.

data_elements.name: uncertaintyBudgetRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the uncertainty budget or evaluation method that produced the stated uncertainty.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The uncertainty attached to a single result is a small set of numeric fields plus a reference. The uncertainty budget itself is a method-level document owned by the procedure model; holding a copy here would create a second budget that could diverge from the validated one.

findings.name: Metrological traceability declaration
findings.description: How the record declares that the result is related to a stated reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, by reference to the calibration and reference-material evidence in force at the time of observation.

questions.text: To which stated metrological reference is this result traceable?
answer_data: Reference identifier (SI unit realisation, certified reference material, reference procedure, conventional scale)
Whether the reference is internationally recognised

questions.text: Which calibration of the observer or measuring system was in force when the observation was made?
answer_data: Calibration validity interval covering the act
Indicator of whether the act fell inside the validity interval

questions.text: Is any part of the traceability chain unestablished or broken, and how is that disclosed?
answer_data: Disclosure text carried with the result

questions.text: Which certified reference materials or reference measurements underpin the chain for this determination?
answer_data: Reference material identifiers and certificate references
Assigned value and its uncertainty as certified
Lot or batch identity where relevant

data_elements.name: metrologicalReference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the stated reference to which the result is traceable, with its issuing authority.

data_elements.name: calibrationInForceRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the calibration record valid at the moment of observation, with the covering validity interval.

data_elements.name: traceabilityChainCompleteness
data_elements.description: Statement of whether the traceability chain is unbroken, with any identified gap and its consequence for comparability.

data_elements.name: referenceMaterialRef
data_elements.description: References to certified reference materials underpinning the determination, with certificate references.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Calibration certificates and reference-material certificates are governed artifacts of the calibration and reference-material models, with their own issuance, validity and revocation lifecycles. This finding records only which of them were in force and whether the chain is complete, so it must not carry copies of them.

findings.name: Reference ranges, interpretation and conformity statements
findings.description: How a result is turned into a judgement: the reference range or specification limit it was compared against, the resulting interpretation code, and, where a statement of conformity is issued, the decision rule identifier and the risk basis behind it.

questions.text: Against which reference range or specification limit was this result compared, and for which population or condition does that range apply?
answer_data: Reference range or limit values with units
Source and version of the range or specification

questions.text: What interpretation was recorded for the result, and using which code list?
answer_data: Interpretation code (for example high, low, within range, out of specification)

questions.text: If a statement of conformity was issued, which decision rule was applied and where is it defined?
answer_data: Decision rule identifier and definition reference
Whether measurement uncertainty was taken into account and how
Guard band or acceptance limit applied
Specification or standard the statement refers to

questions.text: What level of false-accept or false-reject risk does the applied decision rule carry, and who accepted it?
answer_data: Stated risk level or probability of false acceptance
Whether the rule was requested by the customer or inherent in the specification

data_elements.name: referenceRange
data_elements.description: Reference range or specification limits used for comparison, with units and applicable condition.

data_elements.name: interpretationCode
data_elements.description: Coded interpretation assigned to the result, with its code list reference.

data_elements.name: conformityStatement
data_elements.description: Recorded statement of conformity naming the results it applies to and the specification met or not met.

data_elements.name: decisionRuleRef
data_elements.description: Identifier of and reference to the decision rule applied, including the guard band and stated risk basis.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The judgement recorded here is a set of coded values and references. The decision rule is defined and approved elsewhere, and the test report or certificate that publishes the conformity statement is a deliverable of the reporting model, so no artifact is created at the level of a single observation record.

bundles.name: Time, Place and Context
bundles.description: The temporal frame that makes a value locatable in time, the resampling semantics that make it safe to aggregate, and the spatial and environmental context in which it was obtained.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SOSA and SensorThings all separate phenomenon time from result time and admit a distinct valid time, and the OGC Timeseries Profile shows that a value cannot be correctly resampled without interpolation and aggregation semantics. SSN adds operating conditions as a context of validity. These are distinct decision surfaces and are grouped apart from the result.

layers.name: Temporal Frame
layers.description: The several distinct times attached to an observation and the semantics governing how the value behaves across time.

findings.name: Phenomenon, result, valid and ingestion time
findings.description: How the record distinguishes the time the observed phenomenon applies to, the time the result became available, the interval over which the result is asserted to be valid, and the time the record was captured or ingested, each with an explicit offset.

questions.text: To what instant or interval in the real world does this result apply?
answer_data: Phenomenon time instant or interval with explicit offset
Whether it is an instant or an interval
Precision or granularity of the stated time

questions.text: When did the result become available, and separately when was it captured into this record store?
answer_data: Ingestion or capture time with explicit offset
Whether ingestion time is system-assigned and immutable

questions.text: Over what period is this result asserted to remain valid for use?
What clock and offset were in force at the observing location, and how are local-time ambiguities resolved?
answer_data: UTC offset in force at the act
Time zone identifier where local civil time matters
Clock synchronisation source and known drift

data_elements.name: phenomenonTime
data_elements.description: Instant or interval in the real world to which the result applies, expressed with an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: resultTime
data_elements.description: Instant at which the result became available, expressed with an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: validTime
data_elements.description: Interval over which the result is asserted to be usable.

data_elements.name: ingestionTime
data_elements.description: System-assigned instant at which the record was captured into the store, distinct from result time.

data_elements.name: clockContext
data_elements.description: UTC offset and time zone in force at the observing location, with the synchronisation source and known drift.

findings.inline_only_rationale: All temporal context is a small set of timestamp fields plus a clock-context object. It is queried and compared as data, never rendered or exchanged as a standalone object, and materialising it would break the atomicity of the record.

findings.name: Aggregation, interpolation and sampling regime
findings.description: The semantics that determine how a value may be resampled, aggregated or compared: whether it is instantaneous, averaged, accumulated or cumulative, over what duration, and how interim values between observations may be inferred.

questions.text: Does this value describe an instant or an interval, and if an interval, over what duration was it aggregated?
answer_data: Statistical function applied (mean, maximum, total, count)
Alignment of the duration to the stated phenomenon time

questions.text: What interpolation type governs inference of values between this observation and its neighbours?
answer_data: Whether the type is inherited from the series default
Prohibition on interpolation where the type is undefined

questions.text: Is the value cumulative or a reset-prone running total, and what is the accumulation start reference?
At what nominal frequency or sampling regime was the series producing this observation operating?
answer_data: Deviation of this observation from the nominal regime

data_elements.name: aggregationDuration
data_elements.description: Duration over which the value was aggregated, with the statistical function applied.

data_elements.name: interpolationType
data_elements.description: Coded interpolation type governing inference of interim values, with the source of the code list.

data_elements.name: cumulativeFlag
data_elements.description: Indicator that the value is a running total, with the accumulation start reference.

data_elements.name: samplingRegime
data_elements.description: Nominal sampling interval and regime type in force for the producing series, with any deviation for this observation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are interpretation flags and durations carried on the record so that a single observation remains safely resamplable in isolation. The series that supplies the defaults is a separate aggregate with its own identity, so this finding holds effective values only and produces nothing storable.

layers.name: Spatial and Environmental Context
layers.description: Where the observation applies and under what conditions the observing system was operating.

findings.name: Observation location, geometry and spatial reference
findings.description: How the record states the position or extent the result applies to, distinguishing the location of the observer from the location of the feature or sample, and always naming the coordinate reference system and vertical datum.

questions.text: To what position or spatial extent does the result apply, as distinct from where the observer stood?
answer_data: Statement of which geometry the value is attributed to

questions.text: Which coordinate reference system, vertical datum and epoch express these coordinates?
answer_data: Coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic

questions.text: What positional uncertainty attaches to the stated geometry, and how was it obtained?
answer_data: Whether the position is measured, surveyed or nominal

questions.text: Was the location inherited from a station, site or sample record rather than measured for this observation?
answer_data: Effective date of the inherited position
Risk note where the source position may have changed

data_elements.name: resultGeometry
data_elements.description: Geometry or observed area to which the result is attributed.

data_elements.name: observerPosition
data_elements.description: Position of the observer at the time of the act, where it differs from the result geometry.

data_elements.name: spatialReferenceContext
data_elements.description: Coordinate reference system, vertical datum, coordinate epoch and axis-order convention for all geometry on the record.

data_elements.name: positionalUncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty of the stated position with the positioning method that produced it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Geometry and its reference frame are structured values on the record. Station, site and sample geometry are owned by the corresponding entity models; this finding records what was effective for this observation and flags inheritance rather than storing a spatial document.

findings.name: Operating and environmental conditions of validity
findings.description: The conditions under which the observing system was operating and the environment surrounding it, which bound the applicability of any stated system capability such as accuracy, resolution or detection limit.

questions.text: Were the observing system's declared normal operating conditions satisfied at the time of the act?
What environmental context surrounded the observation and could plausibly bias the result?
answer_data: Environmental descriptors with values and units
Reference to the environment record owned by the station or facility model

questions.text: Under which validity context does the stated accuracy, resolution or detection limit hold for this observation?
answer_data: Whether this observation falls inside that context

questions.text: Was the system operating in a degraded, suboptimal or survival regime, and how is that disclosed with the result?
answer_data: Reference to the fault or maintenance record

data_elements.name: operatingConditionsAtAct
data_elements.description: Conditions under which the observing system was operating at the time of the act, with a within-range verdict against declared normal conditions.

data_elements.name: environmentalDescriptor
data_elements.description: Environmental descriptors surrounding the observation, each with value, unit and source.

data_elements.name: capabilityValidityRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the system capability statement and the validity context under which it holds for this observation.

data_elements.name: operatingRegimeCode
data_elements.description: Coded operating regime (normal, suboptimal, survival, degraded) in force during the act.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Capability statements, siting classifications and maintenance records belong to the observing-system and facility models. This finding contributes only the conditions effective at the act and the verdict against declared capability, which are fields on the record.

bundles.name: Quality, Validation and Lifecycle
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected, what quality judgements have been recorded against it, and who is responsible for it.
bundles.rationale: FHIR makes observation status a mandatory modifier element, QARTOD shows quality flagging as a documented layer distinct from the value, MHRA requires original records and controlled amendment, and PROV-O supplies the responsibility model. Together these form the trust surface of an observation record and are separated from the measurement content.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: The states an observation record can occupy and the controlled transitions between them.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The lifecycle states of an observation record from provisional capture through review to final, amended, superseded or retracted, and the rules governing which transitions are permitted, by whom and with what evidence.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle status of this record, and what does that status permit a consumer to do with it?
answer_data: Status code and its governing code list
Permitted consumer uses at that status
Whether the status is a modifier that changes result meaning

questions.text: Which transitions out of the current status are permitted, and what precondition does each require?
Who is authorised to move this record between statuses, and how is that authorisation evidenced?
answer_data: Separation-of-duties constraint where review is required

questions.text: Does this record represent a real-time provisional value or a delayed-mode reviewed value, and are both retained?
answer_data: Whether the provisional value is retained alongside the reviewed value
Reference linking provisional and reviewed records

data_elements.name: recordStatus
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle status of the record, drawn from a governed code list and treated as meaning-changing.

data_elements.name: statusTransition
data_elements.description: Record of a status change with source status, target status, instant, responsible agent and precondition satisfied.

data_elements.name: processingMode
data_elements.description: Whether the record is a real-time provisional value or a delayed-mode reviewed value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status and its transition history are coded fields on the record. The tamper-evident audit trail that independently attests to those transitions is owned by the electronic-records model, so this finding must record state without producing or claiming an audit artifact.

findings.name: Amendment, correction and supersession
findings.description: How a result that must change is handled: whether by amendment in place with a reason, by issuing a superseding record, or by retraction, always preserving the prior content and the reason for change.

questions.text: Which change mechanism applies to this record: amendment, supersession or retraction?
answer_data: Effect on the previous record's status

questions.text: What reason is recorded for the change, and is it classified as a correction, reprocessing or reinterpretation?
answer_data: Reference to the triggering finding or investigation

questions.text: How is the superseded content preserved and made retrievable after the change?
answer_data: Prohibition on obliterating the prior value

questions.text: How are consumers of the superseded value informed that it has changed?

data_elements.name: changeMechanism
data_elements.description: Coded mechanism by which the record's content was changed.

data_elements.name: changeReason
data_elements.description: Recorded reason and classification for the change, with a pointer to the triggering finding.

data_elements.name: supersedesRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the record version this one replaces, and the inverse pointer from the replaced version.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Amendment is expressed by a mechanism code, a reason and version pointers. The preserved prior content lives as an earlier version of the same record rather than as a distinct artifact, and downstream notification is executed by the distribution model, not here.

layers.name: Quality Assessment
layers.description: Quality judgements recorded against the observation and the evidence supporting them, recorded but never evaluated here.

findings.name: Quality flags and quality-control outcomes
findings.description: How quality judgements produced by external quality-control procedures are attached to the record: the flag value, the code list it comes from, which test produced it, when, and by which agent, without this model owning the tests or their execution.

questions.text: What quality flag is recorded against this result, and from which flag code list and version?
answer_data: Flag code list identifier and version
Whether the flag is primary or secondary level

questions.text: Which quality-control test or test suite produced that flag, and where is the test defined?
answer_data: Reference to the quality-control model that owns the test
Test outcome per test where a suite was run

questions.text: When was the flag assigned and by which agent or service?
answer_data: Flag assignment instant with explicit offset
Whether assignment was automated or manual

questions.text: When several flags disagree, which prevails for consumption and how is the disagreement preserved?

data_elements.name: qualityFlag
data_elements.description: Quality flag recorded against the result, with its value, code list, level and meaning.

data_elements.name: qualityTestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the quality-control test or suite that produced the flag, with the parameters in force.

data_elements.name: flagAssignment
data_elements.description: Instant, agent and mode (automated or manual) of flag assignment.

data_elements.name: flagPrecedenceOutcome
data_elements.description: Prevailing flag after applying the precedence rule, with non-prevailing flags retained.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Flags are coded outcomes recorded on the record. Test definitions, thresholds, execution and re-evaluation belong to the quality-control model; carrying an evaluation artifact here would imply ownership of the evaluator, which this model explicitly does not have.

findings.name: Validation and verification evidence references
findings.description: How the record points to the evidence that supports its acceptance: control results, replicate or duplicate observations, blanks, spikes, proficiency-test outcomes and review sign-offs, each held by the model that owns it.

questions.text: Which control, blank, spike or replicate observations support the acceptance of this result?
answer_data: Whether each control passed its acceptance criterion

questions.text: Against which acceptance criteria was this result judged, and where are those criteria defined?
answer_data: Criterion values in force at the act

questions.text: Was the record reviewed and released, by whom and on what date and time?
answer_data: Pointer to the signature record held by the records system

questions.text: Was the procedure verified as fit for purpose in this laboratory for this matrix before the observation?
answer_data: Whether this observation falls inside the verified scope

data_elements.name: supportingObservationRef
data_elements.description: References to control, blank, spike or replicate observations that support acceptance of this result.

data_elements.name: acceptanceCriterionRef
data_elements.description: References to the acceptance criteria applied, with the values in force at the act.

data_elements.name: reviewRecord
data_elements.description: Reviewer reference, review instant and outcome, with a pointer to the signature held by the electronic-records system.

data_elements.name: methodVerificationRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the verification study establishing fitness for purpose, with the scope it covers.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Every item here is a pointer to evidence owned elsewhere: control observations are themselves observation records, acceptance criteria belong to the method model, and signatures belong to the electronic-records system. Materialising an evidence pack here would copy other models' records and create a second, unmanaged source of truth.

layers.name: Provenance and Responsibility
layers.description: Where the record came from, what it was derived from, and who is accountable for it.

findings.name: Provenance chain and derivation
findings.description: How the record states what generated it, which prior entities it used or was derived from, and how the original acquisition record is preserved so that the reported value can be traced back to what the instrument or observer actually produced.

questions.text: Which activity generated this record, and what did that activity use as input?
answer_data: Activity start and end instants with explicit offsets

questions.text: Which prior observations or entities was this result derived from, and by what transformation?
answer_data: Transformation or algorithm reference and version
Whether the derivation is reversible or lossy

questions.text: Where is the original acquisition record, and how is the reported value shown to correspond to it?
answer_data: Correspondence statement between original and reported value
Any processing applied between the two

questions.text: Has this record been reprocessed, and which processing version produced the current value?
answer_data: Prior processing versions and their outputs

data_elements.name: generatingActivityRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the activity that generated the record, with its start and end instants.

data_elements.name: derivedFromRef
data_elements.description: References to source observations or entities from which this result was derived, with the transformation applied.

data_elements.name: processingVersion
data_elements.description: Identifier of the processing version that produced the current value, with prior versions where reprocessed.

artifacts.name: Original acquisition record
artifacts.description: The original record captured at the moment of acquisition, in the form in which the observer or instrument produced it, retained unaltered so that the reported result can be traced back to it. Corrections never overwrite it; they create a new record version that references it.
media_or_form: transcribed field or bench sheet capture
true copy of an original record with its verification statement
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the acquisition-system record key (for example run, batch or injection sequence) qualified by the acquiring system identifier; where the acquisition system issues no key, a digest-addressed identifier is minted by the adopting Dimension and the parent observation identifier plus sequence position is retained as a composite fallback.

findings.name: Ownership, attribution and responsible agents
findings.description: Who owns the record, who is attributed as its producer, which organisation is the authoritative source for which part of it, and who may be contacted about it.

questions.text: Which organisation owns this record and is accountable for its correctness?
answer_data: Effective date of ownership and any transfer history

questions.text: To whom is the observation attributed, and does that differ from the owner?
answer_data: Difference statement between owner and producer
Delegation relationship where an agent acted on behalf of another

questions.text: Which organisation is the authoritative source for each part of the record when several contribute?
Who is the responsible contact for questions about this observation, and how is that contact kept current?

data_elements.name: owningOrganisationRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the organisation accountable for the record, with the effective interval of ownership.

data_elements.name: attributedAgentRef
data_elements.description: References to the agents to whom the observation is attributed, with their roles and any delegation.

data_elements.name: authoritativeSourceMapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from parts of the record to the organisation that is authoritative for each, with conflict-resolution rule.

data_elements.name: responsibleContactRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the contact record for enquiries about this observation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ownership and attribution are reference fields pointing at organisation, agent and contact records maintained by directory models. Copying those records here would duplicate an external register that changes on its own schedule.

bundles.name: Governance, Access and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record is protected and retired, how it is expressed for exchange without losing meaning, how its identifiers resolve across systems, and how it declares its membership in larger collections.
bundles.rationale: DCAT governs access rights, licence and versioning for published data; MHRA imposes retention and archiving duties; SensorThings, FHIR and OMS provide independent encodings that this model must be projectable into. These are governance and projection concerns, deliberately separated from measurement semantics so that storage and interface remain projections.

layers.name: Access and Retention
layers.description: Classification of the record for disclosure and its binding to a retention and disposition policy.

findings.name: Access classification and disclosure constraints
findings.description: How the record declares its sensitivity, the licence or access rights under which it may be used, and any constraint arising from personal, commercial or security sensitivity of the observation or its subject.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must nominate a single master system of record for observation identifiers and declare it before any record is registered; where several producing systems exist, the mapping from producing system to master identifier must be published, not inferred.

The Dimension must bind, per observation programme, the governing retention policy, the applicable data-integrity regime and the accepted unit code system and version, since none of these can be defaulted safely across regions or sectors.

The Dimension must declare which external registries are authoritative for observable properties, procedures, features of interest, units and quality-control tests, and must record the version pinned at the time of each observation rather than resolving against a moving target.

The Dimension must define the lifecycle status code list and its permitted transitions, including whether provisional real-time values are retained alongside reviewed values, before enabling amendment or supersession.

The Dimension must state whether it operates under an accreditation or regulatory regime that imposes uncertainty reporting, decision-rule disclosure or audit-trail duties, and must name the responsible authority.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per adopting Dimension for locally minted surrogate identifiers, kept clearly separate from the namespaces of the master systems and external registries the model references. Never mint a local identifier inside a namespace governed by another authority, and never rewrite an external identifier to fit a local pattern. Where a governed IRI exists for a referenced concept, carry it verbatim alongside any local key. Namespace segments must be stable and free of dates, environment names or version numbers, so that a record exported from one deployment resolves identically in another.
registry_links: Unit code registries: UCUM code system with its version, and QUDT unit and quantity-kind vocabularies where dimensional reasoning is required.
Observable property and quantity-kind vocabularies nominated by the Dimension, with the version pinned per observation.
Observing procedure and test-method registers, including the version executed and the verification scope in force.
Quality-control test registers and their flag code lists, such as programme-specific test suites and their published flag conventions.
Coordinate reference system and vertical datum registers for any geometry carried on the record.
Organisation, agent and contact directories used for ownership, attribution and responsible-contact references.

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form of a record is the format-neutral element set defined by this model; any JSON, XML, RDF, tabular or document projection is derived and must not be treated as authoritative.
All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds present and an explicit offset; a value whose offset is genuinely unknown uses the -00:00 convention rather than being coerced to Z.
Numeric result values are stored at the resolution actually determined; display rounding is applied at projection time and never written back into the stored value.

Unit codes are canonicalised as the pair (code system identifier and version, code string) using the case-sensitive form where the code system distinguishes case; a bare unit string without its code system is not canonical.
References are canonicalised to the identifier plus the scheme that governs it; a dereferenceable URL may be carried in addition but never replaces the identifier.
Ordered collections such as result components and payload parts are canonicalised with an explicit zero-based index; ordering must not depend on serialisation order.
patch_rules: A released record is patched by creating a new version, never by mutating the released version in place; the prior version remains retrievable.
Every patch names the changed elements, the change reason, the change classification and the authorising agent; a patch without a reason is rejected.
A patch may not alter the original acquisition record, the ingestion time or the identity of the observation act.
Changing the observable property, the observing procedure or the ultimate feature of interest is not a patch: it produces a new observation record, because the measurand is no longer the same.
Adding a later quality flag or a later interpretation is an additive patch that must not remove or overwrite the earlier flag or interpretation.
Replacing a surrogate identifier with a newly available authoritative identifier is an additive patch that retains the surrogate as an alternate identifier.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, an alternate identifier scheme or a new alignment declaration is backward compatible.
Tightening a cardinality, narrowing a code list or making an optional element required is breaking and requires a new model version and a migration statement.
Changing the meaning of an existing element, including redefining a status code or a flag value, is breaking even when the element name is unchanged.
A domain profile may constrain but may not relax this model's required elements, and may not redefine phenomenon time, result time or ingestion time.
Alignment to an external standard may be added or revised without breaking this model, provided existing mapping-loss notes are retained rather than silently corrected.
Deprecated elements are retained for at least one full model version with an explicit deprecation marker and a stated replacement.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the declared system of record for the observation, such as a laboratory information management system result key, an observing service observation key or a clinical result identifier; this identifier takes precedence whenever it exists and must be carried verbatim.

Governed global identifier or IRI issued by a normative registry or namespace, such as a resolvable observation IRI under a governed namespace or a persistent identifier assigned by a recognised data authority, used when no master-system identifier exists.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, recorded with an explicit surrogate marker and its minting namespace so it can be superseded additively once an authoritative identifier appears.

A phenomenon time, result time, sample number, file name, run sequence or any date value is never an identifier; such values may only participate as qualifying components of an explicitly scoped composite key alongside a real identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds always present and an explicit offset or Z; a value whose offset is genuinely unknown uses -00:00 rather than being defaulted to UTC, and fractional seconds are recorded only where the producing system genuinely resolves them. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately and never conflated: phenomenon time is the event time in the observed world, result time is when the result became available, valid time is the interval over which the result is asserted usable, and ingestion time is assigned by the receiving system on capture, is not writable by producers, and is retained even when it differs from result time by an arbitrary latency.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Where an artifact belongs to an ordered series — payload parts of a split result, or acquisition records within a run, batch or injection sequence — the series position is recorded as an explicit zero-based integer index within the scope of the parent observation identifier, together with the acquiring or storing system that assigned any native sequence key. The native key is preserved verbatim; the index is a local ordering aid and never replaces it. Series position must not be encoded in file names, and gaps in a sequence are recorded explicitly rather than being renumbered.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest with the named algorithm, its byte size and its media form, recorded at the moment it is bound to the observation record. The original acquisition record is immutable once bound: corrections create a new record version that references it, never a rewrite. Encoded representations carry the record version and digest they were projected from, so a received representation can be matched to the exact record state that produced it, and a digest mismatch invalidates the representation rather than the record. Verification of digests is performed by the storing platform; this model records the digest and the verification outcome but does not implement the store.

policies: Semantics are storage-neutral and interface-neutral. JSON, XML, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the canonical element set; no projection may introduce, remove or rename semantics, and any loss introduced by a projection must be recorded as a mapping-loss note.

A value is never published without the context needed to interpret it: measurand, unit or explicit dimensionless assertion, temporal frame with offsets, and either a quality statement or an explicit declaration that none was made. Absence and censoring are always expressed by coded reasons, never by nulls, blanks or zeros.

External standards are treated as alignments, not as conformance claims. Conformance may be asserted only where testing evidence is referenced; otherwise the alignment is marked as asserted and its known conflicts are recorded.

This model records outcomes it does not compute. Quality evaluation, decision-rule execution, audit-trail capture, notification and physical deletion are performed by the models and platforms that own them; recording a reference to any of these never confers ownership of their behaviour.
Corrections are additive. Prior values, prior flags and prior interpretations are retained and retrievable; obliteration of a released value is prohibited regardless of the storage technology in use.

read: Reading a record returns its effective values including those inherited from a container, with inherited values explicitly marked as inherited.
A read must expose lifecycle status, quality flags and any absence or censoring alongside the value; returning a bare value without them is a defect.
Reads of restricted or embargoed records return the record's existence, identity and classification but withhold the payload according to the access decision made by the access-policy model.
Reading a superseded version is permitted and must indicate that a later version exists, with a reference to it.
Reading a disposed record returns its tombstone rather than a resolution failure.
create: A record may be created only with a resolved identity, an observation type, an owning organisation and an initial lifecycle status.
Creation must capture ingestion time as a system-assigned value that producers cannot supply or override.
Creation of a record whose measurand context cannot be bound is permitted only in a provisional status that is explicitly marked as not fit for consumption.
Where the source system supplies no authoritative identifier, a surrogate is minted with an explicit surrogate marker and the minting namespace recorded.
Bulk creation from a series or stream must preserve per-record provenance; it may not attribute all records to a single synthetic act.
update: Released records are never updated in place; an update produces a new version through the amendment or supersession function.
Additive updates — later flags, later interpretations, newly resolved authoritative identifiers, additional alignment declarations — retain all prior content.
Updates that change the observable property, procedure or ultimate feature of interest are prohibited; those produce a new observation record.
Every update records the changed elements, reason, classification, authorising agent and instant with an explicit offset.
Updates are refused while the record is under a hold that the hold's imposing authority has not lifted.
delete: Records are not deleted on request. Disposition occurs only when the retention period bound to the record expires under its governing retention policy and no hold is in force; this model records the decision and its authority, and the adopting Dimension's records policy owns and executes the destruction.

The retention binding is evaluated separately for the record, its result payload and its original acquisition record, since these may carry different periods; the payload may not be destroyed while a policy still requires the record it belongs to, unless the policy explicitly permits payload-only disposition.

On disposition a tombstone is retained carrying only the record identifier, the disposition instant with an explicit offset, the retention policy reference and the authorising agent; the result value, payload, subject references and personal data do not survive.
References from other observation records or collections to a disposed record resolve to the tombstone, so that derivation chains remain honest rather than failing opaquely.

Where deletion is demanded on a legal ground outside retention — for example an erasure right or a security incident — the determination and its execution are owned by the adopting Dimension's data-protection and records policy and by the storage platform; this model records only the resulting disposition decision and tombstone and never performs, verifies or attests the destruction itself.
A hold suspends disposition entirely; disposition attempted against an unexpired hold is refused and the refusal is recorded.

roles.name: Data Quality Officer

Maintain the flag precedence rule and adjudicate disagreements escalated from records.
Verify that flags recorded on records carry test, agent and instant attribution.

roles.name: Dimension Registrar
responsibilities: Declare the master system of record, the surrogate namespace and the pinned versions of external registries.
